title: OPERATION HOLLOW BELL
skeleton: covering force must hold a garrison's whole attention on a false objective for a fixed window while the order to stop believing in the diversion must be written before it begins
inspiration: Operation Fortitude, 1944 (a diversion sustained on a fixed clock to hold an enemy's attention away from the real movement)
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. {TARGET_FACTION} has run the basin for fourteen months. The garrison is a reinforced battalion: one BattleMech company (12 machines, Regular), one armor company (10 vehicles, a Vedette and Scorpion mix), and a motorized infantry company on checkpoint duty. {NPC:opfor-commander} keeps a tidy post with a fast quick-reaction force, the QRF. Nine days ago, {NPC:intel-source}'s couriers timed that QRF for the third time. It has never taken more than three minutes to roll from the alarm. Treat three minutes as reliable, and plan for the night it finally slips.

{EMPLOYER} is responsible for {CONVOY_SIZE} civilians: SLDF dependents, dockyard technicians, and two HPG maintenance families. They have hidden for eleven weeks in a fish-packing plant east of the basin. A DropShip lands at a worked-out strip mine 60 kilometers east at T+20:00 on the operation clock and holds the pad for exactly 75 minutes. The garrison must not look east during that window. Your job is to give them a louder reason to look west.

The diversion target is the tank farm: {TANK_SPHERES} bulk hydrogen storage spheres. They fuel the garrison's vehicles and the {TARGET_FACTION} aerospace detachment at the airfield. The farm sits at the far end of the causeway, 11.3 kilometers of elevated road across reclaimed salt marsh. It is the only armor-rated route between the cantonment and the farm. Wheeled and tracked vehicles cannot cross the marsh at all. BattleMechs can, but slowly and at risk: unmarked dredge pits run up to 9 meters deep, and the old channel is bottomless. So whoever holds the causeway sets how fast the QRF can reach the farm. That is the core problem. Dockworkers claim, from hearsay in two separate accounts, that garrison engineers have pre-rigged demolition charges on the No. 4 span. It is unconfirmed, but plan as if it is true.

One civilian detail sets the start time. About 41 workers staff the tank farm until 22:00 local, so the operation clock starts no earlier than 22:30. The spheres past the cut-off valves can be destroyed without torching the whole farm. But the blast reaches far: overpressure modeling puts the workers' housing line, 900 meters south, right at the edge of the damage radius. There is a safe margin, but it is thin. The diversion has to be loud, and every shot near the spheres has to be precise.

objectives.primary: Hold the garrison QRF's attention and combat power west of the cantonment from T+0:00 through T+75:00 of the operation clock.
objectives.secondary: Destroy a minimum of 4 storage spheres at the tank farm without igniting the farm field (workers' housing line 900 m south).
objectives.bonus: Exfiltrate with zero BattleMechs lost AND the causeway intact and unblocked — the causeway is wanted for a future operation.

complications.name: Pre-Laid Demolition on Span 4
complications.text: If the rumored charges exist, the garrison can drop the No. 4 span on command. That re-routes their armor — but it also cuts your fastest exfiltration east and strands anything west of the gap.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On garrison escalation (turn 8+ or armor commitment), roll for span demolition. If dropped: causeway impassable at midpoint; exfil through marsh at 1 hex per turn with bog-down checks each turn.

complications.name: Civilian Shift Overrun
complications.text: The 22:00 shift end slips on average twice a week. If workers are still inside the farm perimeter at T+0, the collateral margin collapses and every shot near the spheres is a wager.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll at setup: on 1-2 (d6), 41 civilians remain on site for the first 6 turns. While present, any area-effect or missed attack within the farm rolls on a stray-fire table; civilian casualties advance the campaign reprisal track by 2.

complications.name: Aerospace Pair at the Airfield
complications.text: Two {TARGET_FACTION} interceptors hold strip alert at the garrison airfield. Launch-to-overhead is 22 minutes from hard alarm. They cannot see into the marsh fog but they own the causeway.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From T+22:00, one strafing run per turn against any unit on the causeway or open hardstand until AA fire or fog forces them off.

complications.name: Marsh Fog After 02:00
complications.text: A ground fog forms over the salt marsh most nights after 02:00 local. It blinds both sides. It also makes the dredge pits a navigation problem instead of a map feature.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After the 02:00 mark, sensor and visual range capped at 300 m for all units off the causeway; piloting checks for marsh movement worsen by 1.

decisionPoints.name: The Shape of the Noise
decisionPoints.context: A diversion has to convince the garrison the threat is real. How loud you make it determines how much the garrison commits against you — and what comes hunting you afterward.

options.title: Demolition Raid on the Spheres
advantages: Unmistakable: the garrison commits the QRF, the second lance, and the armor company west
Secondary objective achieved in the same action
Hard alarm starts the aerospace clock on YOUR schedule
disadvantages: Maximum reaction: you will be fighting a reinforced company by T+30:00
Stray-fire risk against the housing line under time pressure
Aerospace pair arrives while you are still decisively engaged
options.consequence: The convoy window is fully covered, but your exfiltration is a fighting withdrawal. Expect to trade armor plate for minutes.

costs.resource: demolition stores: 12 corps-requisition charges, the battalion's full quarterly draw
costs.risk: fighting withdrawal against a reinforced company: projected 2-4 weeks depot time per engaged 'Mech

options.title: Feint with Decoy Traffic
advantages: Low commitment: ECM lance plus dismounted charges on the perimeter wire
Easy break-contact; unit preserved for the next operation
No collateral exposure at the spheres
disadvantages: May draw only the QRF lance — the armor company stays mobile and east remains an option for the garrison
Secondary objective abandoned
If the garrison reads the feint, the convoy axis gets their full attention inside 40 minutes
options.consequence: Convoy coverage is probabilistic, not guaranteed. If the deception holds you win cheaply; if it breaks the evacuation is in a footrace.

costs.resource: ECM expendables and decoy transmitters: one-use draw, not replaceable in theater
costs.risk: if the feint is read, the convoy axis takes the garrison's full attention inside 40 minutes

options.title: Causeway Ambush at the Dredge Narrows
advantages: Controls the QRF's clock exactly — they cannot reach the farm except past you
Best defensive ground in the basin: flanks secured by marsh
Forces the garrison to choose between the causeway fight and the open east
disadvantages: You are fixed in place for the duration; disengagement under pressure is poor
If Span 4 drops behind you, the ambush position becomes a pocket
The second lance can flank via the northern ford given 35 minutes
options.consequence: Maximum control, minimum flexibility. The diversion succeeds almost automatically — and your company carries the whole weight of the garrison's answer.

costs.resource: ammunition: an estimated 60-80 percent of combat load spent holding the narrows
costs.risk: if Span 4 drops behind you, the whole lance is trapped with no way out and no rescue

decisionPoints.name: The Last Fifteen Minutes
decisionPoints.context: At T+60:00 the convoy is either loading or it is not, and you will not know which. You have to write the break-contact order now, calmly and in advance — not later, under fire.

options.title: Break on Schedule at T+60
advantages: Maximum margin against the T+75 hard deadline
Exfil route options still open: causeway or marsh edge
disadvantages: If the convoy slipped 15 minutes, the garrison's attention is released early
Feels like leaving the job unfinished; it sometimes is
options.consequence: Discipline preserved. If the evacuation ran late, the failure fork is in play through no fault of the gun line.

costs.risk: if the lift slipped 15 minutes, the failure fork opens — priced at a second extraction under {TARGET_FACTION} security sweep

options.title: Hold Until Confirmed Lift Signal
advantages: The diversion ends only when it is no longer needed
Convoy coverage is absolute
disadvantages: The signal relay crosses 60 km of occupied basin; silence may mean a dead relay, not a grounded ship
Every minute past T+60 the exfil options narrow by one
options.consequence: Certainty for the convoy bought with uncertainty for the company. Plan the marsh route, because the causeway will not still be yours.

costs.resource: exfiltration corridor: the causeway is forfeited — the marsh route is the only door left
costs.risk: marsh exfil in fog: 1-in-3 bog-down per 'Mech by staff estimate, recovery assets nil

options.title: Phased Withdrawal by Lance
advantages: Half the force preserved early, half maintains the noise
Garrison sensors still read an engagement through T+75
disadvantages: The staying element fights at half strength against a building tide
Two exfil corridors to deconflict in fog and darkness
options.consequence: The compromise costs coordination. If the staying lance is overrun, the saved lance carries that ledger home.

costs.resource: combat power: the staying lance fights the build-up at half strength for 15-plus minutes
costs.risk: overrun exposure: 4 machines and their crews if the garrison's second wave arrives early

entries.event: Perimeter alarm at the tank farm; garrison TOC notified.
QRF lance (4 BattleMechs) departs cantonment west along the causeway.
QRF lance reaches causeway midpoint (Span 4 / dredge narrows).
QRF lance at tank farm perimeter; contact report drives full alert.
Evacuation DropShip grounds at the strip mine, 60 km east. Pad dwell: 75 minutes.
{TARGET_FACTION} aerospace pair overhead the causeway corridor.
Second 'Mech lance and armor company (10 vehicles) committed west.
Garrison posture reassessment: eastward sweeps become available again.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Break contact by T+75:00. The DropShip lifts at T+95:00 whether or not it gets a confirmation signal. Any unit still in a hard fight west of the causeway at T+75:00 has to walk home through the marsh, in fog, against a garrison that is no longer fooled.

opforSketch.composition: Reserve-grade {TARGET_FACTION} garrison battalion. QRF: one light/medium BattleMech lance (Regular). Follow-on: second mixed lance plus an armor company of Vedette and Scorpion equivalents (Regular). Motorized infantry (Green) at fixed posts only. Strip-alert aerospace pair. Generator should weight speed over tonnage and keep total commitment phased, not massed.
opforSketch.behavior: Sequenced commitment doctrine: the commander reinforces in waves and dislikes uncovered flanks. Pursues a withdrawing raider only to the causeway midpoint without armor support. Treats the tank farm as the obvious prize and the east as a backwater until evidence forces a re-read.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN SLIP
forks.trigger: Convoy lifts with zero interception and the diversion force exfiltrates intact.
forks.consequence: The evacuation network passes {EMPLOYER} a standing pipeline: two further hidden groups on {WORLD}, locations pre-surveyed. A follow-on extraction is offered with friendly ground knowledge banked.

forks.name: OPERATION GLEANER
forks.trigger: The garrison breaks east before T+60:00 or the DropShip is forced off the pad.
forks.consequence: The convoy scatters into the strip-mine workings with garrison infantry cordoning. A salvage extraction under air patrol must be mounted within 72 hours, before {TARGET_FACTION} security sweep teams arrive from the capital.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND BELL
forks.trigger: Convoy lifts but the diversion force takes losses or leaves the causeway dropped/blocked.
forks.consequence: Garrison alert state rises for 5 weeks and the basin road net is checkpointed. The unit's next operation on {WORLD} runs at +1 threat band and without the causeway shortcut.

storyElementSeed: Rain on the marsh. A technician wipes condensation off a fuel gauge with one glove and writes the number on the back of a ration sleeve, because the clipboard soaked through an hour ago.

phases.name: PHASE I — MOVEMENT TO CONTACT
phases.lead: The company moves into its attack positions after the 22:00 shift clears the farm and before the 02:00 fog. Put every machine on firm footing you have checked by eye. Confirm the causeway layout in person, not off the map. Then measure the real distance from your gun positions to the housing line, 900 meters south, so you know which shots are safe before you fire them.

dataBlock.Causeway: 11.3 km elevated roadway, sole armor-rated route between cantonment and tank farm
dataBlock.Span 4 demolition: UNCONFIRMED — basis: dockworker hearsay, two independent tellings
dataBlock.Marsh trafficability: impassable to vehicles; BattleMechs slow, unmarked dredge pits to 9 m
dataBlock.Civilian shift: 41 workers on site until 22:00 local; operation clock starts no earlier than 22:30
dataBlock.Collateral margin: workers' housing line 900 m south of the sphere field

phases.name: PHASE II — THE DEMONSTRATION (T+0:00 TO T+60:00)
phases.lead: From the first alarm the company has one task: be the most credible threat on {WORLD} and hold the QRF, the second lance, and the armor company looking west while the convoy loads 60 km east. The noise must read as an attack on the tank farm, not as a screen for the east.

protocol.Lift confirmation: codeword MILLWHEEL, sent twice on 38.5 MHz through the strip-mine relay when the DropShip lifts loaded
protocol.Relay failure rule: silence past T+60:00 is treated as a dead relay, not a grounded ship — the break-contact decision does not wait on the channel
protocol.Abort broadcast: codeword COLD FORGE, any channel, in clear: the convoy is blown and the diversion converts to immediate exfiltration

sidebarKernel.kernel: The QRF has been clocked three times and has never beaten three minutes from alarm to movement. Treat that as the one number on this map that has never been wrong — and plan for the night it finally is.

phases.name: PHASE III — BREAK CONTACT
phases.lead: Breaking contact is a controlled move, not a retreat. Garrison sensors must still read a growing raid through T+75:00 while the company slips out along whatever route the fight has left open. Write the order before the operation and follow it without changes under fire.

routes.name: Route COPPER — the causeway deck
routes.desc: Withdrawal along the elevated roadway at best speed, clearing Span 4 before the garrison's follow-on armor reaches the midpoint.
routes.tradeoff: The fastest exit in the basin and the only one the garrison can close with a single demolition order — if Span 4 drops, COPPER ends at the midpoint of 11.3 kilometers with marsh on both sides.

routes.name: Route REED — the marsh edge
routes.desc: Surveyed footing along the salt marsh fringe, 1 hex per turn with bog-down checks, visibility capped at 300 m in fog after 02:00.
routes.tradeoff: No garrison unit will follow — and one failed piloting check at a dredge pit converts a withdrawing 'Mech into an abandoned one.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Write the T+60 break order now, in the cold, and sign it. The version composed at T+59 under flare light is always worse and always late.

resourceGates.lackingText: No corps demolition draw available: charges improvised from strip-mine explosives — add 1 day of preparation, and the brief prices the sphere kill at 2 confirmed instead of 4.

title: OPERATION SLATE SKY
skeleton: recon element must deliver a verified count between storm cycles that blind both sides while the weather that conceals the approach is also the only door out
inspiration: long-range reconnaissance patrols across uncrossable terrain (e.g. the Long Range Desert Group, 1941) — counts delivered by elements that lived where the enemy could not watch
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. This world only stays livable because machines tame its weather. For two centuries, six regional Storm Inhibitor stations broke up the cyclone belts. Since the coup, two of the six have gone dark: their crews were conscripted and their parts stripped, and nobody fixed it because nobody is left who cares. That count is 21 days old, from {NPC:intel-source}, so treat it as a rough picture. The result is the Gap: a 60-kilometer corridor between the still-working stations where uncontrolled storms roll west to east on a roughly {STORM_CYCLE}-hour cycle. Inside a storm cell, winds hold at 140 kph, you cannot see, sensors reach under 200 meters, and radio is dead. Both sides go blind in it. That is why the Gap is the one approach to the aerodrome that {TARGET_FACTION} ground radar cannot cover: their radar is as useless in there as yours.

The aerodrome is a former SLDF auxiliary field. {TARGET_FACTION} has spent seven months turning it into an aerospace staging base. The last orbital pass was 33 days ago, so its numbers are stale: it counted 19 aircraft in open revetments, 6 to 9 more under construction, and what looks like bulk fuel storage on the northwest apron. In five weeks {EMPLOYER} moves a loyalist convoy through this sector. Whether the convoy lives depends on three questions: is the real count 19 interceptors or 28, are the fuel tankers real, and are the new revetments hardened. Orbital photos cannot answer those. A ground team can.

This is a true reconnaissance raid: the mission is the count, not the kill. You need photographs of the aircraft types and numbers, the fuel storage, the anti-aircraft positions, and the garrison's ground posture. One report claims Partisan-pattern AA vehicles, but that is a single 26-day-old sighting at a refueling stop, so it is not confirmed. Getting into a fight counts as failure, with one exception: a target so valuable it changes the whole picture. That case is handled in the decision annex, not by a snap call in the field.

Plan around the cold and the clock. The plateau surface sits near minus 20 Celsius, which limits observers on foot to 40-minute shifts. The storm cycle gives you a wall of weather to hide behind going in, and a wall you must beat coming out, and it will not bend to your schedule. A team that misses its window spends 40 hours stranded on a frozen plateau with an interceptor wing for company.

objectives.primary: Deliver verified counts and photographic documentation of the aerodrome: airframes by type, revetment hardening, fuel bunkerage, AA positions, ground-force posture.
objectives.secondary: Map the Gap transit route — storm-edge navigation marks, dead ground, and the inhibitor maintenance road — for reuse by follow-on operations.
objectives.bonus: Remain entirely undetected: no contact reports, no sensor logs, no missing patrols. The convoy's safest corridor is one {TARGET_FACTION} never knew was surveyed.

complications.name: Storm Cycle Drift
complications.text: The cycle runs roughly {STORM_CYCLE} hours, but it drifts up to 6 hours either way as the dead stations throw the pattern off. So the window you planned around is only an estimate, not a schedule.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll storm arrival at mission start: ±6 hours on the planned cycle. During storm passage: no radio, no aerospace either side, movement halved, visual/sensor range 200 m.

complications.name: Weather Radar as Early Warning
complications.text: The aerodrome's meteorological radar is run by people who used to do air-defense work. It cannot classify a contact in clutter, but it flags movers on the open hardpan in clear conditions.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any unit moving in the open during clear weather risks a detection roll per turn; active sensor use by the recon element doubles the risk.

complications.name: Inhibitor Maintenance Convoy
complications.text: A civilian crew of 11 vehicles transits the Gap road every 4 days, servicing the two surviving stations on this side. They carry a {TARGET_FACTION} liaison and a working radio.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Encounter check on the Gap road each transit day. Civilian contact starts a 4-8 hour report clock; the liaison's radio cuts that to 30 minutes unless jammed or the storm is up.

decisionPoints.name: Window or Wall
decisionPoints.context: The Gap can be crossed three ways, and each one pays for its concealment with something different — control, speed, or the safety of the team.

options.title: Ride the Storm Wall
advantages: Masked from radar and aerospace for the entire approach
Arrive as the cell clears — best photographic light of the cycle
Any pursuit must wait out the same weather
disadvantages: Navigation hazard: piloting checks in zero visibility along the trailing edge
No communications during the approach; an abort cannot be ordered
Timing error of 2 hours strands the element inside the cell
options.consequence: Maximum concealment, zero recall. The element is alone from line of departure until the wall passes.

costs.resource: command authority: zero recall — no abort can be ordered between line of departure and wall clearance
costs.risk: one failed piloting check in zero visibility is a machine abandoned in the Gap

options.title: The Clear Gap Between Cells
advantages: Full visibility for navigation and overwatch
Communications available throughout; abort and contingency orders possible
Fastest transit: the whole approach in 9 hours
disadvantages: The weather radar sees the hardpan as well as you see the field
Aerospace pairs fly in exactly this window
Detection on approach burns the corridor for the convoy planning that follows
options.consequence: Speed and control purchased with exposure. Every hour in the open is a coin flip you cannot weight.

costs.risk: detection on open hardpan burns the corridor for the convoy — the mission's whole value staked once per exposed hour

options.title: Foot Observation Post by Cargo Crawler
advantages: A 4-man OP is deniable in a way a BattleMech is not
{OP_EMPLACE}-hour emplacement allows observation across a full garrison routine cycle
'Mech element stays 30 km out, beyond the radar problem entirely
disadvantages: {OP_EMPLACE} hours to emplace; the answer arrives late in the planning window
If the storm closes early, the OP is cut off — the crawler cannot beat the wall and the 'Mechs cannot reach them through it
40-minute exposure rotations in minus 20 Celsius limit continuous observation
options.consequence: The most reliable count and the most fragile element. If the cycle drifts wrong, four people winter on the plateau within rifle distance of the enemy.

costs.resource: cold-weather stores: 4-man OP draw for 5 days at minus 20 Celsius on 40-minute rotations
costs.risk: a 6-hour cycle drift strands the OP one full storm cycle — 40 hours within rifle distance of the field

decisionPoints.name: Target of Opportunity
decisionPoints.context: The orbital assessment flagged possible fuel tankers on the northwest apron. If they are real and present, the convoy's threat picture changes — and so might the mission.

options.title: Photograph Only
advantages: Mission discipline preserved; detection risk unchanged
The count remains the product, and the count is what the convoy needs
disadvantages: Fueled interceptors have legs; the convoy corridor must be planned wider and slower
The opportunity may not recur
options.consequence: The recon stays a recon. The convoy planners get the tanker problem with full information and no smoke on the horizon to give the mission away.

costs.risk: the fueled interceptor wing stays whole: the convoy corridor must be planned wider and slower

options.title: Sabotage via the OP Team
advantages: Quiet: a contaminant mixed into the fuel shows up weeks later as engine failures, not as an attack
No weapons fire and no alarm — it looks like a {TARGET_FACTION} maintenance failure
disadvantages: Puts the OP team inside the perimeter fence: capture risk is real and personal
If discovered in the act, the garrison knows a ground element walked in — sweeps follow for weeks
Requires 3 additional hours on-site past the planned exfil mark
options.consequence: A bet that quiet hands beat loud guns. Win, and the interceptor wing rots from inside. Lose, and the Gap route is burned with four people still in it.

costs.resource: special stores: one fuel-contaminant package, single use — plus 3 hours on-site past the planned exfil mark
costs.risk: capture of 4 OP personnel inside the perimeter fence, and the Gap route burned with them

options.title: Extend Observation 24 Hours
advantages: Confirms whether the tankers cycle through or are based at the field
Pattern-of-life data multiplies the value of every photograph
disadvantages: Another full day against the storm clock and the rotation limits
Consumables and cold-weather endurance run to their margins
options.consequence: Patience pays off. The intelligence gets sharper, but the exfil window narrows to a single storm cycle.

costs.resource: consumables and cold-weather endurance run to zero reserve at exfil
costs.risk: the exfil window narrows to a single storm cycle with no second chance

entries.event: Detection event: radar flag, visual sighting, or maintenance convoy report reaches aerodrome operations.
Interceptor pair launches (clear weather only); first sweep of the hardpan corridor.
Ground QRF — wheeled armor platoon — departs the field perimeter for the Gap road.
BattleMech lance off strip alert; methodical sweep of dead ground begins.
Garrison settles into sustained search posture; OP discovery odds rise each cycle the element remains.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: From any detection event, the recon element must be inside the storm wall or off the plateau not later than T+35:00. In clear weather the air pair finds a BattleMech-sized contact on open hardpan in under 15 minutes — and the next storm cell is the only door out that {TARGET_FACTION} cannot close.

opforSketch.composition: Aerospace-centric {TARGET_FACTION} garrison: interceptor squadron — actual strength {AIRFRAME_COUNT} airframes once the new revetments fill (weather-limited), one wheeled armor platoon as ground QRF (Regular), one BattleMech lance on 40-minute strip alert (Regular), 4-6 Partisan-pattern AA vehicles on field perimeter (UNCONFIRMED). Generator should weight aerospace and sensors over ground mass.
opforSketch.behavior: Responds with sensors and aircraft first, ground units second and reluctantly. Will not pursue into storm cells under any circumstances. Logs and reports every anomaly to sector command — the lasting threat is the report, not the response.

forks.name: OPERATION THIN CORRIDOR
forks.trigger: Verified counts delivered with no detection event logged.
forks.consequence: The loyalist convoy transits the sector on a corridor plotted around the aerodrome's real reach. The unit is credited with the corridor and offered the escort tasking at favorable terms.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG WAY ROUND
forks.trigger: Counts not obtained, or obtained too degraded to plan against.
forks.consequence: The convoy reroutes 11 weeks around the sector. To cover the delay, {EMPLOYER} orders a fuel-denial raid against the aerodrome's bunkerage — the loud version of the question this mission was meant to answer quietly.

forks.name: OPERATION WEATHER EYE
forks.trigger: Detection event logged and reported up the {TARGET_FACTION} net.
forks.consequence: A second interceptor squadron deploys to {WORLD} within 3 weeks. The recon element must exfiltrate under active air search across two storm cycles, and every operation in the sector runs at +1 threat band for 6 weeks.

storyElementSeed: The observation rotation changes in silence: one set of gloved hands passes the lens cloth to the next, and the count on the slate stays where it is — 19 airframes, two revetments uncounted, wind rising.

phases.name: PHASE I — TRANSIT OF THE LEVASSEUR GAP
phases.lead: The Gap is crossed on the storm's schedule, not the unit's: the method chosen in the decision annex executes against a cycle that drifts up to 6 hours either way. Navigation marks, dead ground, and the inhibitor maintenance road are logged on the way in — the map made during transit is half the secondary objective.

dataBlock.Storm cycle: {STORM_CYCLE} hours nominal, drift to plus or minus 6 hours
dataBlock.In-cell conditions: sustained wind 140 kph, visibility zero, sensor range under 200 m, radio dead

phases.name: PHASE II — THE COUNT
phases.lead: Observation is the mission: aircraft by type checked against the 33-day-old count of 19, revetment hardening, the northwest-apron fuel storage, AA positions, and ground posture. Log every photograph with its time, bearing, and light. A photo nobody can verify is worthless.

protocol.Transmission discipline: no emissions from the OP except one 8-second burst at 0410 local on 121.2 MHz, daily
protocol.Compromise signal: any burst outside the 0410 window means the OP is compromised and the exfil clock starts at that mark
protocol.Recovery signal: two green flares at the crawler rendezvous, 30 seconds apart — visual only, nothing on the net

sidebarKernel.kernel: Cold soak is the enemy nobody briefs: at minus 20, actuator seals stiffen after 6 hours static, and the first movement turn tells the weather radar exactly what just woke up. Budget a warm-up cycle into every displacement.

phases.name: PHASE III — BEATING THE WALL
phases.lead: Exfiltration is timed against the next storm cell: inside the wall or off the plateau not later than T+35:00 from any detection event. The element that misses its window spends 40 hours on a frozen plateau with an interceptor wing for company, and the plan treats that as a failure mode, not an option.
