resourceGates.lackingText: Option renders locked: REQUIRES DEPOT DRAW — no cargo crawler or 5-day cold-weather OP kit on unit books, and minus 20 Celsius does not improvise.

title: OPERATION LONG FALLOW
skeleton: interdiction force must starve a garrison for a fixed season from pre-stocked caches while the signature of each strike decides whether civilians or the force itself absorbs the answer
inspiration: partisan rail-and-canal interdiction behind an occupation (e.g. the Belorussian rail war, 1943)
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The plateau garrison sits on high ground and is fed from the river. {TARGET_FACTION} moves {BARGE_TONNAGE_SHARE} percent of the garrison's supplies by barge, up the lock flight: five locks that lift traffic 64 meters from the lowland river port to the plateau railhead. Manifests copied by {NPC:intel-source}'s dock-clerk circuit are only six days old and reliable. They put weekly throughput at 2,900 tons: fuel, rations, ammunition, and the spare parts that keep a reserve-grade armor battalion running. The locks are civilian-run, as they were before the coup. The crews did not choose their cargo.

{EMPLOYER}'s intent is a 90-day interdiction campaign: make the plateau garrison burn through its reserves and stop trusting its roads, ahead of a separate operation elsewhere in the sector that is not your concern and will not be briefed. You will operate from four pre-stocked caches holding {CACHE_DAYS} days of consumables, with no resupply. The terrain problem is the lock stair: the lock flight and its switchback service road are the only river-gorge crossings a BattleMech can use, and only at the No. 2 and No. 5 lock crests. A garrison blockhouse overlooks the pool between locks 3 and 4 and reports in on a 90-minute check-in cycle.

Understand the reprisal pattern before you fire the first shot, because it is part of the terrain. After every strike so far blamed on 'civilian-assisted banditry,' {TARGET_FACTION} security has detained residents of the nearest commune — six after the first incident, eleven after the second. The number of detentions scales with how much civilian help the enemy assesses was involved. Strikes that look like the work of a professional military force draw troop sweeps; strikes that look like local resistance draw hostage-taking. Every operational choice in this campaign has to factor in civilian detentions, and the plan does not get to pretend otherwise.

The garrison: one reserve armor battalion (Regular, under-strength), one BattleMech lance held at the plateau aerodrome, two VTOLs flying daily air sweeps, and a {TARGET_FACTION} security field office that is better at its job than the garrison is at soldiering. They will adapt. After the third convoy strike, expect doubled escorts and randomized scheduling. You win this campaign by burning their reserves faster than they burn your caches — and by still being undetected on day 89. Pickup runs day 88 to day 93. There is no day 94.

objectives.primary: Reduce garrison resupply throughput across the lock corridor by 40 percent or more, sustained across the 90-day campaign window.
objectives.secondary: Preserve the intelligence network: end the campaign with {NPC:intel-source}'s dock-clerk circuit uncompromised and the four cache sites undiscovered.
objectives.bonus: Force the garrison to commit its BattleMech lance to convoy escort duty for 30 consecutive days or more, fixing it away from the aerodrome.

complications.name: The Reprisal Index
complications.text: {TARGET_FACTION} security answers strikes with detentions, scaled to assessed civilian involvement. Past a threshold, the communes stop talking to anyone — including the dock-clerk circuit that feeds you manifests.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each strike adds 1-3 to a reprisal track based on how 'local' it reads. At {REPRISAL_THRESHOLD} accumulated points, the intelligence network goes dark for 14 days: no manifests, no warning of escort changes.

complications.name: Conscripted Barge Crews
complications.text: The tugs are crewed by civilians under requisition orders. Killing them is both a moral ledger entry and an operational one — dead crews mean {TARGET_FACTION} naval ratings replace them, and ratings carry radios.
complications.mechanicalEffect: ROE: disable tugs and barges, not crews. Attacks on barge traffic roll stray-fire checks; any crew casualties add 2 to the reprisal track and accelerate escort doubling by one week.

complications.name: Adaptive Escorts
complications.text: The garrison learns. After the third successful strike, convoy escorts double, scheduling randomizes, and the VTOLs shift from fixed sweep lanes to manifest-keyed coverage.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From strike 4 onward: ambush setup rolls worsen by 2, and each ambush risks VTOL response from turn 3 instead of turn 6.

complications.name: Cache Discovery Risk
complications.text: Every visit to a cache leaves sign — track plates, thermal scarring, disturbed ground. {TARGET_FACTION} security field teams read sign for a living.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each cache used more than twice rolls for security discovery on every subsequent use. A discovered cache is ambushed, not emptied.

decisionPoints.name: What Breaks First
decisionPoints.context: The supply corridor can be attacked at the lock machinery, in the water itself, or on the road. Each choice starves the garrison in a different way — and each one is paid for by a different group.

options.title: Disable Lock 3 Machinery
advantages: One action starves the plateau for an estimated 5-7 weeks of repair
No sustained exposure: a single engineering strike, then silence
Garrison must divert troops to guard a repair site for weeks
disadvantages: Grain moving DOWN the locks stops too — the upland communes go onto ration within 12 days
Reads as professional sabotage: {TARGET_FACTION} security sweeps follow, and the reprisal track jumps by 2 immediately
The repaired lock will be garrisoned permanently afterward
options.consequence: The fastest strangulation and the largest civilian bill. The campaign objective is met early and the countryside pays the difference.

costs.resource: reprisal track: +2 immediately; upland communes on ration inside 12 days
costs.risk: professional-sabotage security sweep reaches the strike grid within 40 hours

options.title: Selective Channel Mining
advantages: Sustainable: tonnage drops 30-40 percent and stays down while sweeping continues
Sweep operations consume garrison engineer hours every 9-12 days, indefinitely
Reads ambiguous — could be old war stocks, could be local — keeping the reprisal calculus low
disadvantages: Requires repeated access to the water: more exposure events than any other approach
Mine stocks are finite: 9 patterns in the caches, no more coming
A swept channel is a temporary victory by definition
options.consequence: The patient option. The garrison bleeds slowly and the campaign lives or dies on whether nine patterns of mines can be made to last ninety days.

costs.resource: mine stocks: 9 patterns in the caches — the campaign's entire allotment, no resupply
costs.risk: one exposure event per emplacement run, repeated across 90 days

options.title: Leave the Water — Hit the Road Convoys
advantages: The locks stay untouched and deniable; barge crews and communes stay out of the line of fire
Road ambushes play to BattleMech strengths in the gorge country
Forces the garrison to choose between road escorts and lock security
disadvantages: Direct combat exposure every strike: the armor battalion gets practice and so do their gunners
Road tonnage is the minority share — the corridor objective needs more strikes to reach 40 percent
Each engagement is a fresh chance to be identified as SLDF regulars, with everything that follows
options.consequence: Cleanest hands and hardest fighting. This trades sabotage for a straight attrition fight, and your machines are the ones with no repair depot behind them.

costs.resource: cache consumables: each ambush spends an estimated 3-5 days of the cache ledger
costs.risk: attrition without a depot: armor damage taken is carried unrepaired to day 90

decisionPoints.name: The Blockhouse Question
decisionPoints.context: The garrison blockhouse over the pool between locks 3 and 4 watches the only night crossing of the lock stair. Over 90 days of operations, you will have to cross it more than once.

options.title: Take It Quietly with Infantry
advantages: Permanent night access to both banks once held
The blockhouse's own logs and codebooks come as salvage
disadvantages: The 90-minute check-in cycle means a missed report brings a platoon in 15 minutes
Holding it requires either a permanent detachment or a convincing radio deception, sustained for weeks
options.consequence: One sharp risk traded for standing freedom of movement — and a deception that must work 16 times a day, every day, until pickup.

costs.resource: manning: a permanent detachment or a radio deception worked 16 times a day until pickup
costs.risk: one missed check-in brings a platoon in 15 minutes

options.title: Bypass via the Weir Crest
advantages: No contact, no alarm, no deception to maintain
The weir route is unwatched precisely because it is bad ground
disadvantages: BattleMechs ford the pound at 2 meters' depth: actuator flooding checks every crossing
Single-file, slow, and unusable when the river runs high after rain
options.consequence: The engineering risk replaces the security risk. A flooded actuator 40 km from the nearest cache is a strategic event, not a maintenance note.

costs.resource: transit time: the single-file ford adds 4 hours to every east-bank operation
costs.risk: actuator flooding check each crossing — one failure is a strategic loss, not a maintenance note

options.title: Never Cross at Night
advantages: The blockhouse stays irrelevant; zero added exposure
Operational pattern stays simple and sustainable
disadvantages: The east bank target set is halved; reaching 40 percent interdiction takes longer
Daylight operations trade the blockhouse problem for the VTOL problem
options.consequence: Discipline over reach. The campaign accepts a smaller map and bets that the west-bank targets are enough.

costs.resource: target set: the east bank forfeited after dark — the 40 percent objective leans entirely on west-bank tonnage
costs.risk: daylight operations trade the blockhouse problem for the VTOL problem

entries.event: Strike initiated: convoy contact, mine detonation, or sabotage discovered. Garrison TOC alerted.
Both VTOLs airborne; sweep lanes converge on the strike grid.
Reaction lance begins descent from the plateau aerodrome via the switchback road.
Blocking positions established at the No. 2 and No. 5 lock crests; the Stair closes.
{TARGET_FACTION} security field team on site; sign-reading and commune interviews begin within hours.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Per strike: break contact not later than T+12:00. Any engagement still running at T+14:00 races the descent lance to the Stair crests, and the Stair is the only way home. Campaign: consumables end at day {CACHE_DAYS}; the pickup window is day 88 to day 93, and there is no day 94.

opforSketch.composition: One reserve armor battalion (Regular, under-strength — Vedette and Scorpion equivalents with thin infantry support), one BattleMech lance at the plateau aerodrome (Regular), two armed VTOLs, {TARGET_FACTION} security field office (Veteran, threat-multiplier). Generator should escalate escort weight over campaign time rather than fielding mass early.
opforSketch.behavior: Convoy-protection doctrine that learns: fixed patterns for the first three strikes, then doubled escorts, randomized scheduling, and manifest-keyed air cover. Security forces answer with detentions and sign-reading, not pursuit. The garrison never night-fights if it can cordon and wait for daylight.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET GRANARY
forks.trigger: Interdiction target met with network and caches intact at day 90.
forks.consequence: The plateau garrison draws down its war reserve to 30 days and reports the corridor unreliable. The sector transfer operation proceeds on schedule, and the unit is extracted with the dock-clerk circuit still alive for the next campaign.

forks.name: OPERATION SCATTERED SEED
forks.trigger: Network rolled up or two or more caches discovered before day 60.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} security sweeps own the lowlands. The unit must reach the highland emergency pickup on half consumables, moving only at night, with the reprisal detentions running ahead of it like a bow wave.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND SOWING
forks.trigger: Interdiction achieved but the network is burned or the reprisal track crossed its threshold.
forks.consequence: The tonnage objective stands; the human cost does too. A follow-on campaign next season must rebuild caches and contacts from nothing, on a world where the communes now count the price of helping before they open a door.

storyElementSeed: Cache inventory by red light: rounds counted into cloth bundles of ten, the tally whispered once across the crate and written nowhere.

phases.name: PHASE I — ESTABLISHMENT (DAYS 1-14)
phases.lead: Before the first strike: survey both banks of the lock stair, proof all four cache sites, and watch the corridor through two full convoy cycles without touching it. The campaign's safety margin is built in these two weeks or never.

dataBlock.Lock flight: 5 locks lifting 64 m, river port to plateau railhead
dataBlock.Blockhouse check-in: 90-minute cycle; one missed report brings a platoon in 15 minutes
dataBlock.Cache ledger: 4 sites, {CACHE_DAYS} days of consumables, 9 mine patterns, no resupply
dataBlock.Pickup window: day 88 to day 93 — there is no day 94

phases.name: PHASE II — INTERDICTION (DAYS 15-75)
phases.lead: Strikes run on the rhythm the reprisal index permits, not the rhythm the tonnage target wants. Each action is priced in three currencies before it is ordered: cache days spent, reprisal points added, and what the garrison learns from the wreckage.

protocol.Manifest drops: the dock-clerk circuit leaves copies in the culvert at switchback marker 7, every 4th day
protocol.Danger sign: a chalk X on the culvert lip means {TARGET_FACTION} security has visited — the drop is dead for 14 days, no exceptions
protocol.Network silence rule: two consecutive empty drops means the circuit is dark; operate on direct observation only until it signals again

sidebarKernel.kernel: The ledger is the campaign: {CACHE_DAYS} days of consumables against 90 days of war, and every ambush spends 3 to 5 of them. Read the cache book before the target list, every time.

phases.name: PHASE III — QUIET RUNNING (DAYS 76-93)
phases.lead: Strikes end by day 75. The last two weeks are spent breaking the unit's own pattern: dead-end movements for the sign-readers, caches stripped in reverse order of discovery risk, and the pickup approached as if the campaign's whole ledger rides on it — because it does.

assetDetails.detail: Runs the dock-clerk circuit that copies the manifests. That six-day-old, reliable intelligence is the campaign's best asset and its most fragile. The clerks are put at risk by the reprisal track, not by anything they do wrong. You protect them by keeping the reprisal track low, not by warning them.

Civilians under requisition orders, crewing tugs they did not choose. ROE is machinery, never people: a dead crew is replaced by {TARGET_FACTION} naval ratings who carry radios, and the reprisal track moves 2 for every name on the casualty list.

title: OPERATION STILL WATER
skeleton: security detail must stop saboteurs wearing its own uniform while the facility's underside cannot be fully watched and the rules for the decisive four seconds must be written weeks early
inspiration: wartime counter-sabotage of strategic industry (e.g. guarding a heavy-water plant against trained infiltrators, 1943)
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. This world builds warships. The drive-ring segments for the orbital yards are cast on the ground at the foundry annex, and the annex dies without the No. 2 coolant intake on the tailrace — a 240-meter spillway channel running along the annex's southern boundary. If the intake pumps stop, the crucible line has to be drained within 3 hours 40 minutes, or the molten metal freezes solid in place and the line is gone for an estimated 14 months. Both claimants to the realm want the yards working. Both would rather see them shut down than working for the other side. {EMPLOYER} holds the annex; your unit holds the intake.

The threat is not a battalion. It is six people with shaped charges and a survey map. Sabotage cells aligned with {TARGET_FACTION} have made two attempts in five weeks — one turned back at the wire, the other discovered afterward as a charge that failed to fire on pump house 3's manifold. Assessment attributes the work to a detached recon element operating in regular-army uniform, helped by insiders within the annex ({NPC:opfor-commander} is the working name for whoever runs them; their identity is unknown). The people probing your wire trained at the same NCO academies yours did. Nobody here switched armies. Everybody chose a side.

The terrain problem is underneath you. The storm-drain galleries run {DRAIN_KM} kilometers beneath the annex. The only drawings are dated 3021 and are known to be incomplete, so the real layout is worse than the map. Three surface crossings span the tailrace: a rail trestle, a service bridge, and a sluice catwalk. All three can be watched. The drains cannot, not fully, not with your numbers. The security element is {SECURITY_ELEMENT} personnel plus one BattleMech lance that is too big for half the places this fight will happen.

The workforce is the other kind of terrain. {WORKFORCE} workers cover three shifts. Eleven days ago a works-council vote split 1,704 to 1,396 on a resolution everyone knew was really about the war. The 1,396 are not enemies. But a few of them will hold a door for the wrong person, and that is all this kind of war needs. A planetary broadcast crew is embedded in the annex by agreement with the employer. Everything your sentries do happens in front of a camera, including the mistakes.

objectives.primary: Keep the No. 2 coolant intake, its pump houses, and the switchyard operational for the 60-day casting run. Zero unrecovered sabotage events.
objectives.secondary: Identify and roll up the insider support: names, access routes, and the courier link to {NPC:opfor-commander}'s element — delivered to {NPC:employer-contact} as evidence, not bodies.
objectives.bonus: End the tasking with the works council's cooperation intact and no incident on the broadcast record that names your unit.

complications.name: The Crucible Clock
complications.text: Casting physics does not pause for investigations. Any interruption to coolant flow starts a 3-hour-40-minute countdown to losing the line — and the saboteurs know the number as well as the foundry engineers do.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any successful sabotage of a pump house starts a hard 3:40 repair clock. Repair requires securing the site AND engineering checks; a second device found on-site (roll) restarts the search but not the clock.

complications.name: The Galleries
complications.text: Twelve-plus kilometers of storm drains, mapped to 3021 standards, with at least 4 unrecorded connections cut by maintenance crews over the decades. Complete sensor coverage is not achievable with the resources assigned.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Infiltration attempts may spawn from drain nodes inside the perimeter. A maximum of 60 percent of nodes can be sensored or grated at any one time; the layout choice is the player's.

complications.name: Cameras at the Wire
complications.text: The embedded broadcast crew has employer protection and an audience. Rough handling of workers, weapons fired near the queue lines, or a body on the trestle will lead the planetary feed within two hours.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each public incident advances an opinion track. At threshold, the employer imposes restrictive ROE (no weapons release without officer authorization) for 10 days.

complications.name: Divided Rosters
complications.text: Six of the security element's own personnel have siblings or spouses in units declared for the other claimant. They are not suspects. They are people doing a job their families consider treason.
complications.mechanicalEffect: When ordered to fire on personnel in friendly-army uniform, affected troops roll a loyalty/morale check; a failure is hesitation, not betrayal — one turn of inaction at the worst possible time.

decisionPoints.name: Posture
decisionPoints.context: Security comes down to a few settings: how visible the posture is, how hard it is, and whose hands are on the gates. Once you set them, you cannot reset them.

options.title: Hard Overt Perimeter
advantages: Deterrence: visible wire, lit crossings, BattleMechs at the trestle ends
Simple ROE, simple sectors, fewest judgment calls at 0300
disadvantages: Shows the attackers where the hard routes are, pushing them into the drains where you are weakest
Looks like an occupation on the broadcast feed; works-council goodwill drops every week
Fixed posts settle into a pattern, and a trained recon team beats a pattern
options.consequence: The wire holds and the war goes underground. Within three weeks, the contest is entirely in the galleries, on the map from 3021.

costs.resource: works-council goodwill: spends down weekly under occupation optics
costs.risk: the threat moves to the drain galleries, where coverage caps at 60 percent

options.title: Covert Depth and Sensors
advantages: Infiltrators are caught in the act, with evidence — the employer's preferred outcome
Low broadcast profile; the annex looks like a workplace, not a front line
Sensor budget concentrated on the drain nodes where the real approach runs
disadvantages: No deterrence: attempts will keep coming, and one will eventually be good
60 percent node coverage means real gaps, chosen by you and findable by them
A catch in the dark at close quarters is a gunfight, not an arrest
options.consequence: The annex stays calm on the surface while the basement becomes a patient, silent contest of map knowledge. Whoever surveyed last, wins.

costs.resource: sensor inventory: the full drain-node budget committed, with the gaps chosen and known
costs.risk: a catch in the dark at close quarters is a gunfight, not an arrest

options.title: Deputize the Works-Council Watch
advantages: 3,000 pairs of eyes that know which doors should be locked and which faces belong
The 1,704 get a stake in the outcome; insider recruitment gets harder
Frees your element to hold the pump houses and the drains
disadvantages: The 1,396 are inside the watch too — your early-warning net has a hostile minority by construction
Council politics enter your security decisions; the broadcast crew will cover every dispute
An armed-civilian incident is the worst possible headline of the contract
options.consequence: Security becomes politics by other means. The net catches more and leaks more, and you will not always know which happened first.

costs.resource: command attention: council politics enter every security decision, on camera
costs.risk: a hostile minority of 1,396 built into the early-warning net by construction

decisionPoints.name: First-Shot Rules
decisionPoints.context: The infiltrators wear the same uniform your sentries do. On the night it matters, a sentry will have about 4 seconds to decide, working from a rulebook you wrote weeks earlier.

options.title: Challenge and Detain
advantages: Prisoners are intelligence, and intelligence ends this contract early
Defensible on camera, in court, and at the works council
disadvantages: A challenge is a free first shot for a team that came to fight
Veteran recon troops do not freeze at a challenge; yours might
options.consequence: The honorable rule and the expensive one. Plan the casualty evacuation route before you plan the press release.

costs.resource: medevac standby: one vehicle and crew held back around the clock
costs.risk: the challenge is a free first shot for a team that came to fight — paid in sentries, not C-bills

options.title: Fire on Positive Hostile Act Only
advantages: No dead night-shift fitter who took a shortcut — the irreversible mistake is ruled out
Cleanest legal and political posture available
disadvantages: A placed charge IS the hostile act; you find out when the search does
Grants the infiltrators every approach up to arm's reach of the manifolds
options.consequence: The crucible clock becomes the real sentry. The rule protects everyone except the pumps.

costs.risk: a placed charge is found at search speed against the 3-hour-40-minute line-death countdown

options.title: Pre-Authorized Fire in Exclusion Zones
advantages: The pump houses and drain mouths become genuinely lethal ground after curfew
Removes the 4-second judgment call from a 19-year-old with a rifle
disadvantages: The night a fitter chases a dropped tool past the wire, the rule does what rules do
On the broadcast feed, an exclusion-zone shooting is indistinguishable from a murder
options.consequence: Maximum protection for the machinery, full transfer of moral weight to the order — and to whoever signed it.

costs.resource: workforce night access to the pump houses closed; off-shift repair work slows
costs.risk: one wrong silhouette after curfew is a broadcast-led shooting, priced at the contract plus the media-liability clause

entries.event: Intrusion alarm — sensor trip, sentry contact, or anomaly at a pump house.
Ready section moves; duty officer authorizes search posture.
Mounted QRF rolls; Tailrace crossings sealed (trestle, service bridge, catwalk).
Cordon complete; drain node overwatch shifts to intercept pattern.
Engineering decision point: flood-gate the drain galleries (stops movement below; costs 6 hours of pump capacity margin).
Search transitions to recovery: any breach not retaken by now is assumed to have placed charges.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Any pump-house breach must be retaken and searched within 25 minutes. Past that, assume charges are set and start the 3-hour-40-minute crucible clock whether or not a device has been found — the line drains on schedule or the line dies.

opforSketch.composition: No conventional ladder. Primary: 2-6 person sabotage teams (Veteran), demolitions-trained, operating in friendly-army uniform with current-pattern identification. Support: annex insiders (Green, access only, unarmed). Conditional: a covering recon lance sits OUTSIDE the wire per intelligence now 19 days old, so treat it as likely but unconfirmed; it commits only if a team is trapped. Generator should weight infantry and battle-armor-scale threats; BattleMech contact belongs to the escalation fork, not the base mission.
opforSketch.behavior: Patient and intelligence-led. Probes are reconnaissance until one is rehearsed enough to be an attack. Aborts on uncertainty, never reinforces failure, and prefers the drains and the workforce to the wire. If cornered, fights briefly and professionally toward a pre-surveyed exit.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY DOCK LADDER
forks.trigger: Casting run completes; insider network identified and handed over as evidence.
forks.consequence: Drive-ring segments ship on schedule. The employer extends the contract to escort the segment haul to the mass-driver railhead — higher profile, better terms, and the saboteurs' parent unit now knows your unit's name.

forks.name: OPERATION SCALD
forks.trigger: The intake is lost and the crucible line slags out.
forks.consequence: The annex goes dark for 14 months. {EMPLOYER} orders a compensating raid to seize replacement pump impellers from a storage yard the other claimant holds — the security failure converted directly into an offensive tasking nobody wanted.

forks.name: OPERATION GLASS HOUSE
forks.trigger: A public incident — civilian casualty or broadcast scandal — regardless of the intake's status.
forks.consequence: The unit is reassigned to rearguard convoy duty under hostile public attention. Future contracts on {WORLD} carry a media-liability clause priced against this one's record.

storyElementSeed: Night shift files past the new wire. A fitter holds her badge up to the light without being asked, and the sentry, who knows her by name, checks it anyway and writes down the time.

phases.name: POSTURE (DAYS 1-10)
phases.lead: The first ten days set the dial that cannot be set twice: sensor layout in the galleries, the crossing watch, and the face the security element shows {WORKFORCE} workers and one broadcast camera. Survey before commitment — the drain map is dated 3021, and the other side's copy may be newer.

dataBlock.Tailrace crossings: rail trestle, service bridge, sluice catwalk — all three watchable
dataBlock.Drain galleries: {DRAIN_KM} km, as-built drawings dated 3021, at least 4 unrecorded connections
dataBlock.Node coverage ceiling: 60 percent of drain nodes sensored or grated at any one time
dataBlock.Crucible clock: 3 hours 40 minutes from coolant stop to losing the line

phases.name: THE PROBES
phases.lead: Two attempts in five weeks set the tempo: expect the next probe to test whatever the posture decision left thin. Every probe that is seen and logged — even one that walks away clean — is evidence the roll-up objective needs.

protocol.Challenge discipline: duty word pair changes at 0001 daily, issued at shift muster, never over radio
protocol.Uniform rule: friendly-army uniform plus the correct word pair is still not clearance inside the pump-house exclusion line after 2200 — escort required, no exceptions for rank
protocol.Incident flash: code DRY DOCK on the duty net freezes all crossing traffic and starts the 25-minute retake clock

sidebarKernel.kernel: The failed charge on pump house 3's manifold is the best document in this file. Whoever wired it knew the maintenance schedule — pull the access logs for that week before chasing anyone at the wire.

phases.name: FLASHPOINT
phases.lead: The night it matters lasts under ten minutes and is decided by rules written weeks earlier: the first-shot ruling, the 25-minute retake clock, and whether the duty officer flood-gates the galleries at T+15:00. Run the drill twice weekly until the 0300 version matches the briefed version.

sidebarKernel.kernel: If the clock starts, drain sequence beats heroics: the line survives a controlled 3:40 drain and does not survive an argument about whether the device was real.

assetDetails.detail: Site of the recovered dud charge. The device sat behind the surge damper, reachable only with the access panel unbolted — 11 minutes of undisturbed work by trade estimate. Treat the manifold catwalk as the benchmark for what an insider can reach on a normal shift.

Six of the security element have siblings or spouses in units declared for the other claimant. They are cleared for duty and told so to their faces; post them in pairs with unaffected personnel, and keep them off the challenge points where the friendly-uniform call is theirs alone to make.

Three persons, employer credentials, contractual access to everything outside the pump-house exclusion line. They file at 1800 daily whether or not anything happened. The crew is not hostile; the deadline is.

is-steiner.situation.framing: The annex ledgers say the yards belong to whoever keeps them casting. House Steiner built half its power on exactly this arithmetic: hold the infrastructure, keep the books clean, and let the romantics spend regiments on gestures. The personnel probing the wire wear the same uniform you do — treat that as a logistics fact, not a tragedy. Uniforms are issued; loyalties are declared; both are documented. Write everything down. After this war the auditors arrive before the historians, and they will want the intake's uptime figures, not your feelings about them.

resourceGates.lackingText: Sensor net leased from annex industrial suppliers instead of purchased: 9,000 C-bills per week against the contract, installed by unvetted local technicians — the vetting problem now lives inside your own detection layer.

title: OPERATION SEALED MANIFEST
skeleton: raiders must empty or burn an island stockpile and recross the only rated span before it drops while overstaying converts the objective into a prison
inspiration: commando raid on a fortified causeway depot (e.g. the St Nazaire raid, 1942)
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. A customs audit found the war before the war found the harbor. A routine review of the bonded stores in the harbor roads, opened over a tariff discrepancy, turned up eleven months of falsified manifests. Behind them sat a hidden depot: {GYRO_CRATES} crated BattleMech gyros of assorted classes, an estimated {MUNITIONS_TONNAGE} tons of mixed munitions, and bulk cold-weather actuator lubricant. Officers whose sympathies run to {TARGET_FACTION} stockpiled it all on the bonded-stores island. {EMPLOYER} wants the depot gone before it can equip a battalion. The intelligence comes from {NPC:intel-source}, a customs auditor now housed at unit expense. It is eight days old and only partly reliable, because the manifests themselves are partly false. That cuts both ways: the depot may actually be larger than the paper says.

The bonded island is artificial: 400 by 700 meters of landfill and ferrocrete in the harbor roads, connected to the mainland by the viaduct — 1.9 kilometers of single-track rail viaduct rated at 85 tonnes. That rating is the terrain problem. It means one BattleMech at a time, walking the railway sleepers, 11 minutes per crossing, with nowhere to go if a span is dropped. The mainland garrison has pre-rigged demolition charges on the No. 3 span; engineering assessment says they can drop it 55 minutes after an alarm once they have authorization, and authorization will not be the bottleneck.

The guard detail is the part your briefing cannot make simple. One platoon of regulars holds the island — soldiers who refused recall orders when their parent battalion declared for {TARGET_FACTION}. By their own reckoning they are not deserters; they are obeying the last lawful order they recognize, and their commander ({NPC:opfor-commander}) has twice agreed to parley with harbor officials over rations and mail. They will fight to hold the depot. They may also talk. Fog rolls into the roads on the tide in {FOG_WINDOW}-hour windows at 80 meters' visibility, and the fog does not care which side it helps.

This is an objective raid with a ledger attached: whatever you seize re-equips a loyalist battalion, and whatever you destroy is denied to both halves of an army that will one day be a single army again. Someone will have to answer for tonight in that future army. Plan as though that someone is you.

objectives.primary: Neutralize the bonded-island depot as a war resource: seize or destroy the gyro stock and munitions before mainland forces can intervene.
objectives.secondary: Recover the depot's true ledgers and shipping records — the supply network that filled the island matters more than the island.
objectives.bonus: Resolve the guard platoon without fatalities on either side: parley, withdrawal under arms, or detention. The after-war ledger pays this line best.

complications.name: False Manifests
complications.text: The paper says {GYRO_CRATES} gyro crates. The paper has been lying for eleven months. Crates of ballast were used to balance the books at least once, and possibly the reverse — undeclared stock in the unbonded annex.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll actual contents on arrival within the specifics ranges. On a 1 (d6), 4 of the gyro crates are ballast; on a 6, an undeclared annex holds 30 percent additional munitions tonnage — and a load-out plan sized for the manifest.

complications.name: Harbor Patrol
complications.text: Two patrol boats work the Roads on a 40-minute circuit: light weapons, spotlights, and radios that reach the mainland garrison watch desk directly.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Boats respond to any alarm within 12 minutes. They cannot hurt a BattleMech; their spotlights and contact reports advance the mainland reaction timeline by one step if either boat survives to observe the viaduct.

complications.name: The Standing Parley
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} has met harbor officials twice under flag. A parley before contact is genuinely available — and a failed one tips the island to full alert and the mainland to early notification.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Pre-combat parley option: on success, the guard platoon stands down to barracks under terms; on failure, the island alerts AND the mainland timeline starts at T+0 with the parley itself as the alarm.

complications.name: Civilian Fire Brigades
complications.text: The bond stores are insured, and the harbor's fire brigades are proud, fast, and entirely uninterested in your tactical situation. A fire on the bonded island brings them INTO the engagement area within 20 minutes.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any fire-setting or ammunition cook-off spawns civilian fire-brigade units moving toward the blaze from T+20:00; all fire lanes crossing their approach impose stray-fire checks and opinion-track penalties.

decisionPoints.name: Approach
decisionPoints.context: An artificial island with only one rated crossing is either a fortress or a trap, depending on which side of the viaduct you are standing on when the span drops.

options.title: Walk the Viaduct
advantages: Full BattleMech weight delivered to the objective — nothing on the island argues with that
No dependence on weather, hulls, or third parties
The lance arrives together and leaves together
disadvantages: 11 minutes per machine, single file, on a structure with pre-rigged demolition
The crossing is the alarm: a 'Mech on the sleepers is visible from the mainland watch tower in any weather short of fog
Egress and ingress share one span that you do not control
options.consequence: Decisive force, hostage to a bridge. The whole operation lives inside the 55-minute demolition authorization clock.

costs.resource: crossing time: 11 minutes per machine, single file, in and out, on one rated span
costs.risk: every machine island-side of the No. 3 span at T+55:00 is forfeit — the bridge is the bet

options.title: Hover Assets Across the Roads
advantages: Fast: the full assault element on the island inside 15 minutes
Independent of the viaduct entirely — the demolition charge becomes their problem, not yours
The fog windows make the crossing effectively unobserved
disadvantages: Payload ceiling: armor and infantry, no BattleMechs — the guard platoon's anti-armor weapons stay relevant
The fog window is {FOG_WINDOW} hours and the tide table is not a promise
Loading seized cargo back onto hover transport doubles the extraction time
options.consequence: Speed and surprise, bought by leaving the heavy metal home. If the guard platoon stands and fights, it is a fair fight — which is to say, a failure of planning.

costs.resource: combat power: BattleMechs stay home — the payload ceiling is armor and infantry
costs.risk: the fog window closes on the tide table, and loading seized cargo doubles the extraction time

options.title: Barge Infiltration the Night Before
advantages: An infantry element inside the wire before the first alarm: gates opened, demolition leads cut, guards located
The depot's own cargo handling cranes become your load-out equipment
Cheapest option in fuel, ammunition, and attention
disadvantages: 36 hours of exposure between insertion and H-hour; one curious sentry unravels everything
The element is alone on the island if discovered — no support can reach them in under 25 minutes
Requires a barge, a crew, and a harbor pass, each one a person who can talk
options.consequence: The quiet hand opens the island from inside, or is found holding it. Everything depends on 36 hours of other people's incuriosity.

costs.resource: operational security: a barge master, a crew, and a pass broker — three hired people who can talk
costs.risk: 36 hours of exposure; if discovered, the element is alone on the island for 25-plus minutes

decisionPoints.name: Disposition of the Stores
decisionPoints.context: The depot can be hauled away, burned, or partly taken and partly destroyed. For all three, the clock starts the moment the mainland hears the first wrong noise.

options.title: Gyros Only
advantages: Highest value per tonne and per minute: 35-minute load-out
Gyro stock is the bottleneck resource for any battalion the other side is building
Smallest extraction footprint — one rail consist or two hover runs
disadvantages: The munitions remain: the depot is wounded, not dead
A second operation against an alerted island will cost what this one saved
options.consequence: Surgical and incomplete. The raid pays for itself in gyros and leaves a lighter, angrier depot behind.

costs.resource: load-out window: 35 minutes spent against the 55-minute span clock
costs.risk: the munitions remain — a second operation against an alerted island costs what this one saved

options.title: Full Load-Out
advantages: The depot ceases to exist as a military resource AND your side keeps the materiel
The ledgers, the lubricant stock, the lot — nothing left to argue over
disadvantages: 70 to 85 minutes of loading against a 55-minute demolition clock: the arithmetic only works if the mainland alarm comes late
Requires the viaduct intact for rail extraction — the single most fragile assumption available
options.consequence: Maximum prize at maximum exposure. This option is a bet that the alarm clock is slower than the customs paperwork was.

costs.resource: loading time: 70-85 minutes against a 55-minute demolition clock — the margin must come from a late alarm
costs.risk: rail extraction stakes everything on the viaduct, the single most fragile assumption available

options.title: Destroy in Place
advantages: 8 minutes to set, fastest of the three by an order of magnitude
No extraction tonnage, no viaduct dependence on the way out
Denial is certain in a way that seizure never is
disadvantages: Your own side needs those gyros; denial spends materiel the Commonwealth will want back in two years
A bond-store fire spreads: the civilian brigades come into your engagement area, with cameras behind them
The munitions cook-off makes the island uncrossable for hours — count your own people first
options.consequence: Certainty, paid in smoke. The depot dies tonight and the after-war ledger opens a line item with your unit's name on it.

costs.resource: denied materiel: the gyro stock and munitions the Commonwealth will want back in two years
costs.risk: a bond-store fire pulls the civilian brigades into the engagement area with cameras behind them

entries.event: Alarm on the bonded island: sentry contact, patrol boat report, or watch-tower sighting of movement on the viaduct.
Harbor patrol boats vector to the Roads; mainland garrison watch desk notified.
Boats on station with spotlights; militia armor platoon alerted at the viaduct abutment.
Militia armor at the mainland abutment; viaduct under direct observation and fire.
{TARGET_FACTION} BattleMech lance from the mainland aerodrome rolling; demolition authorization request in channel.
No. 3 span demolition authorized and available for command detonation.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Get every tonne and every machine across the viaduct by T+55:00. At T+55:00 the span drops. After that the bonded island is a trap, with only the tide-window hovercraft route left as a way out.

opforSketch.composition: On the island: one {TARGET_FACTION} regular infantry platoon (Regular, motivated, defensive) with platoon anti-armor weapons and prepared positions among the bond stores. In the roads: two patrol boats (Green crews, light weapons). Mainland escalation: militia armor platoon (Green), then one {TARGET_FACTION} BattleMech lance (Regular) from the aerodrome. Generator should hold mainland forces to the timeline, not the map.
opforSketch.behavior: The guard platoon defends in place and does not sortie; parley is genuinely possible before first blood and impossible after. Mainland doctrine is containment: seal the viaduct, drop the span if in doubt, and let the island problem starve. Nobody on the other side is in a hurry except you.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN BOOKS
forks.trigger: Depot neutralized, ledgers recovered, force extracted before span demolition.
forks.consequence: The shipping records expose the mainland supply network — 3 freight forwarders and a customs officer. {EMPLOYER} offers the follow-on tasking: escort the seized stores convoy and lift the network quietly, before the war does it loudly.

forks.name: OPERATION WET INK
forks.trigger: Raid repulsed or aborted with the depot substantially intact.
forks.consequence: The sympathizer network burns its records and disperses the stores across 9 mainland sites inside two weeks. Finding the depot's successor means operating against an alerted garrison with the customs trail gone cold.

forks.name: OPERATION SPLIT LEDGER
forks.trigger: Stores partially seized or destroyed; span dropped or extraction contested.
forks.consequence: Half the materiel is out, the rest is slag or stranded, and the harbor is a political wound: the brigades fought a fire your raid started. Harbor authority cooperation is withdrawn for 60 days, and the next coastal operation plans around its absence.

storyElementSeed: In the bond office, crate stencils are read by torchlight against a manifest that does not match them, and the sergeant doing the arithmetic licks a pencil stub and starts the count again from the top.

phases.name: PHASE I — THE ROADS
phases.lead: Approach per the decision annex, timed to the tide-fog tables. Whatever the method, the parley question is settled before the first element commits: an offer under flag is possible exactly once, and only before anything has happened that needs explaining.

dataBlock.Viaduct: 1.9 km single-track rail, rated 85 tonnes — one BattleMech at a time, 11 minutes per crossing
dataBlock.Span 3 demolition: pre-rigged; 55 minutes from alarm to authorized command detonation
dataBlock.Fog windows: {FOG_WINDOW} hours at 80 m visibility, on the tide
dataBlock.Harbor patrol: two boats, 40-minute circuit, direct radio to the mainland watch desk

protocol.Parley form: white flag at the pierhead gate, two persons, sidearms holstered, before first blood only
protocol.Terms on offer: stand-down to barracks under arms, rations and mail honored, no disarmament demanded
protocol.Failure rule: a refused parley is the alarm — the mainland timeline starts at the refusal, not at the first shot

phases.name: PHASE II — THE ISLAND
phases.lead: The bonded island is taken or talked over inside the first 20 minutes; either way, the guard platoon question is closed before any crate is touched. A fight still running when the load-out should start has already spent the full-seizure option.

phases.name: PHASE III — THE LEDGERS AND THE LOAD-OUT
phases.lead: The true ledgers and shipping records come out first — they are the secondary objective and they weigh nothing. Then the disposition decision executes against the clock the alarm set, with the stencil-versus-manifest count running as the crates move.

dataBlock.Manifest reliability: falsified for eleven months — the count on the pier is the only true number

sidebarKernel.kernel: Every crate that crosses the viaduct gets a line in the seizure book with time and stencil code. After this war there will be a prize court, and the unit's claim is exactly as good as tonight's handwriting.

phases.name: PHASE IV — THE VIADUCT CLOCK
phases.lead: Egress is arithmetic: 11 minutes per machine, single file, against T+55:00. The withdrawal order of march is written before H-hour, and the last machine in the column is chosen on purpose, not by accident.

assetDetails.detail: Has accepted parley twice over rations and mail and honored the flag both times. Holds the platoon to the last lawful order they recognize; an offer that lets them stand down without the word 'surrender' in it has a real chance, and one that uses the word has none.

The customs auditor — housed at unit expense, frightened, and the only person who can read the depot's double books at speed. Will identify the true ledgers on sight but will not cross the viaduct; bring the records to the mainland abutment, not the auditor to the records.

is-davion.situation.framing: Strip the bond-store politesse: that island is an arsenal assembled by people preparing to shoot at their own army, and the polite word 'sympathies' does not change the tonnage. Take the gyros, spike the rest, and be off the viaduct before the engineers get their authorization. The guards are soldiers obeying a dead order of battle — give them one honest chance to stand aside, document that you gave it, then stop offering.

resourceGates.lackingText: Option renders locked: INSUFFICIENT TREASURY — barge hire, crew, and harbor pass are cash-up-front purchases from people who do not extend credit and do not take paper.

No organic lift for 1,800-plus tons: seized stores transfer to {EMPLOYER} at the pierhead for prize-rate credit (60 percent of assessed value) instead of entering unit inventory — the brief prints the prize-rate figure.

title: OPERATION COLD CHAIN
skeleton: escort must ration one chokepoint's transit slots between two life-critical cargoes on a single hard countdown while enemy stay-behinds spend cheap provocations to burn the hours
inspiration: armed relief convoys into a besieged population under deliberate harassment (e.g. the ground leg of a blockade-relief airbridge, 1948)
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The capital is a ruin now. The strike lanes from the orbital attack overlap in a 6-kilometer arc of fused rubble and radiation hot spots that the survey teams call the glass belt. About {POPULATION} people are still alive north of it. That count comes from ration-card issue records, is 17 days old, and is only a rough figure, because nothing else on {WORLD} can count people anymore. {EMPLOYER} has hired your unit to escort and protect {SERIALS} convoy serials, or loads: food, water purification units, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. They run from the intact secondary landing strip 80 kilometers north, through the belt, to distribution points in the survivor districts. The antibiotics are refrigerated, and that cold chain holds for only 21 days from the landing date. That is the real deadline, and you cannot argue with bacteria.

Two surveyed routes cross the belt. Corridor KALE: 9.8 kilometers, three mapped hot spots, with a radiation dose budget of {DOSE_TRANSITS} crossings per crew per week — exceed it and that crew is off driving duty for a month. Corridor MILLET: 22.4 kilometers, radiologically clean, but with two chokepoints in collapsed underpasses where a single stalled truck stops the whole convoy. Choosing the route is the terrain problem, and you will make that choice fourteen times.

The opposition is small and serious. A {TARGET_FACTION} stay-behind cell has hit distribution points five times in fifteen days, roughly every third day. That pattern is only two days old and reliable. The cell is an estimated 20 to 30 fighters, two light vehicles, and one mortar section; track casts at the fourth attack site suggest one battle armor suit, but that is unconfirmed. They are not trying to steal the food. They are trying to make feeding people cost lives, because a food queue that gets mortared twice stops forming, and a city that stops lining up for rations starves quietly without the enemy firing another round. Separately, organized looters with forged consortium markings work the routes farther up; they want the cargo, which at least makes them predictable.

The crowds have learned the same lesson the mortar crews have. In the first 40 seconds after a round lands, most of the killing is done by the crowd crushing against the barriers, not by shrapnel. Your plan has to solve that problem as seriously as it solves the counter-battery one. The districts have wardens, run by {NPC:resistance-leader}. They can move food faster than you can, while skimming 8 to 15 percent off the top. Work out what that skim buys before you refuse it. Everything here comes down to numbers now. This contract is for professionals who can do that math without flinching and without enjoying it.

objectives.primary: Deliver and distribute all {SERIALS} convoy serials inside the 21-day cold-chain window, with cargo loss under 10 percent.
objectives.secondary: Break the distribution-point attack pattern: locate, fix, or deter the stay-behind cell so that queues can form without casualties.
objectives.bonus: End the contract with a functioning district distribution system that runs without your escort — the consortium's definition of success that outlives the invoice.

complications.name: Dose Budget
complications.text: Corridor KALE is fast and hot. The crews carry dosimeters, the dosimeters keep honest books, and the books say each crew crosses {DOSE_TRANSITS} times a week and no more. Heroics show up as medical downgrades two weeks later.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track KALE transits per crew. Exceeding the weekly budget removes that crew from operations for 30 days; any serial halted in a hot zone longer than 18 minutes counts double against its crew.

complications.name: The Surge
complications.text: A mortared queue does not scatter — it compresses. The first 40 seconds after impact, the barriers do the killing. Crowd-control failures end distribution days as surely as direct hits.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On any attack at a distribution point, roll crowd-surge severity. Weapons fire near the queue automatically maximizes the result and cancels distribution at that site for the day; cancelled days feed the enemy's broadcast line.

complications.name: Forged Markings
complications.text: Looters running consortium-marked trucks intercept cargo upstream of the points — paperwork, vests, the right paint. The fakes are good because the people who painted them used to do it for a living.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Convoy serials and distribution handoffs require identification checks; a failed check diverts 1 serial's partial load. Establishing a code-word system with the wardens negates this after the first incident.

complications.name: Dead Air
complications.text: The strike corridors burned out the civil comm infrastructure, and the belt's rubble eats line-of-sight. Retrans means high ground or airborne relay, and the enemy knows where the high ground is.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Communications blackout zones cover 40 percent of both corridors. Units inside a blackout zone cannot call for QRF support; pre-planned movement schedules substitute for radio contact.

decisionPoints.name: The Route, Fourteen Times
decisionPoints.context: KALE is short and irradiated. MILLET is long and has chokepoints. Whatever route pattern you settle into is the pattern the enemy cell learns to ambush.

options.title: KALE Every Serial
advantages: Fastest turnaround: two serials a day inside the cold-chain window with margin
Hot spots deter dismounted ambush along most of the corridor
Shortest exposure to looter interception
disadvantages: Dose budget consumes crews on a schedule: by week two, driver rotation is the binding constraint
A predictable route is a targetable route — the cell needs only one good day
A breakdown in a hot zone is a casualty event, not a maintenance event
options.consequence: Speed against the bacteria, bought with crews. The cold chain holds and the medical annex fills from the inside.

costs.resource: crew dose budget: drivers consumed on schedule — rotation is the binding constraint by week two
costs.risk: a breakdown in a hot zone is a casualty event, not a maintenance event

options.title: MILLET Every Serial
advantages: Radiologically clean: no dose accounting, no crew burn rate
The underpass chokepoints can be picketed and held as fixed security
Recovery vehicles can operate freely anywhere on the route
disadvantages: 22.4 kilometers means one serial a day: the cold-chain margin shrinks to nearly nothing
The chokepoints are perfect ambush ground, and both sides can read a map
Looters work the long corridor's open stretches with room to maneuver
options.consequence: The careful road, fully spent. Any two bad days — weather, breakdown, attack — and the antibiotics expire in their reefers within sight of the people who need them.

costs.resource: cold-chain margin: one serial a day spends the 21-day window to nearly zero
costs.risk: any two bad days and the antibiotics expire in their reefers within sight of the queue

options.title: Alternate Unpredictably
advantages: No pattern for the cell to plan against; ambush preparation cost doubles
Dose budget spread thin enough to keep every crew operational
Route-denial attacks (rubble, mines) can only close half your options at a time
disadvantages: Double the route-clearance workload, every day, for the whole contract
Scheduling complexity: the wardens' distribution timetable slips, and slipped timetables thin the queues' trust
Mixed exposure means mixed casualties — a little of every cost instead of a lot of one
options.consequence: Operational soundness at administrative expense. The convoys live on a dispatcher's whiteboard, and the dispatcher had better be good.

costs.resource: route clearance doubled, every day, for the length of the contract
costs.risk: slipped distribution timetables thin the queues' trust — and thin queues are the cell's victory condition

decisionPoints.name: The Point
decisionPoints.context: The food has to be handed over somewhere. Where you do it, and through whom, decides who is standing out in the open when the cell's every-third-day attack pattern comes around again.

options.title: Fixed Point at the Tram Barn
advantages: Defensible: hard cover, controlled entries, counter-battery radar with a stable plot
Predictable for the population — queues form because people know where to stand
Scales and ledgers under one roof; accountability the consortium can audit
disadvantages: The mortars have its grid; every distribution day is a pattern-day wager
Crowd density at a fixed point maximizes surge casualties when it goes wrong
The cell gets to rehearse against a stationary target
options.consequence: Order and accountability concentrated into one address — along with every risk the contract contains.

costs.resource: counter-battery radar committed to a single grid for the contract's length
costs.risk: every distribution day is a pattern-day wager at a published address

options.title: Rolling Distribution from Truck Beds
advantages: No fixed grid for the mortar section; the target moves every 40 minutes
Surge risk dispersed across a dozen small queues instead of one large one
Coverage reaches districts too far from the tram barn to walk
disadvantages: Crowd control at twelve makeshift sites with the same escort that struggled at one
Accountability falls apart: counts made off a tailgate are rough estimates, not real tallies
The looters' forged trucks blend into a rolling system perfectly
options.consequence: The mortars lose their grid and the ledgers lose their lines. Fewer people die at the barriers; more cargo dies on the books.

costs.resource: accountability: tailgate counts are estimates, audited against the 10 percent loss ceiling
costs.risk: crowd control at twelve ad-hoc sites with the escort that struggled at one

options.title: Warden Handoff
advantages: The wardens move food faster than any escort schedule — distribution finishes inside the window with days to spare
District-run points draw no crowds of strangers, and the cell's pattern feeds on strangers
Your unit's exposure drops to the corridor runs alone
disadvantages: 8 to 15 percent skim, priced into every serial, visible in every audit
The consortium's accountability clause was written by people who have never been hungry
{NPC:resistance-leader}'s organization becomes the de facto ration authority — power that outlives the contract
options.consequence: The food moves and the books bleed. The skim buys a distribution network, a quieter Belt, and a political question someone else will answer in a year.

costs.resource: skim: 8-15 percent of every serial, visible in every audit and priced against the loss ceiling
costs.risk: the wardens become the de facto ration authority — a political bill that arrives after the invoice clears

entries.event: First mortar round impacts at or near a distribution point.
Crowd surge crests at the barriers. This is the casualty peak, not the impacts.
Counter-battery plot (if radar emplaced) produces a firing grid.
The cell displaces — observed displacement time across five prior attacks is under 5 minutes.
React section reaches the baseplate area; historically it is empty by now.
Distribution either resumes behind reset barriers or the day is lost and the broadcast line writes itself.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Two clocks, both firm. Per transit: any serial stopped in a glass-belt hot zone longer than 18 minutes blows its crew's weekly dose budget. Per contract: the cold chain fails at day 21 from landing. Every refrigerated tonne not delivered by then is wasted, and the cost of that is counted in the medical tents, not the after-action report.

opforSketch.composition: {TARGET_FACTION} stay-behind cell: 20-30 effectives (Veteran), two light utility vehicles, one mortar section, possibly one battle armor suit (UNCONFIRMED). Separate threat: organized looters with technical vehicles and forged markings (Green, motivated by cargo not casualties). Generator should keep the cell small, skilled, and never decisively engaged; the looters provide the contact volume.
opforSketch.behavior: The cell fights the queue, not the convoy: harassment by pattern, displacement under 5 minutes, no decisive engagement ever. It is trying to make relief cost more than abandonment. The looters avoid escorts entirely and hunt paperwork gaps; they will trade fire only when cornered with cargo aboard.

forks.name: OPERATION WARM HAND
forks.trigger: Serials delivered inside the window; distribution pattern held against the cell.
forks.consequence: The wardens pass hard targeting on the stay-behind cell — hide sites, supply caches, the boat that resupplies them. The consortium funds a follow-on strike tasking, and for once the intelligence is fresh and the locals are owed nothing.

forks.name: OPERATION THIN GRUEL
forks.trigger: Two or more serials lost, or the cold chain expires with cargo undistributed.
forks.consequence: Rations cut to 60 percent of plan. The queues thin, then turn. The unit's closing weeks are spent holding the secondary-strip perimeter against unrest the shortfall created — guarding the food that came too late from the people it was for.

forks.name: OPERATION BLACK MARKET
forks.trigger: Diversion traced through unit-hired drivers or escort negligence, regardless of delivery totals.
forks.consequence: Contract penalties invoke the accountability clause. A counter-diversion investigation runs inside the unit's own hiring records while the remaining serials still have to move — and the consortium's auditors ride along.

storyElementSeed: At the head of the queue, a clerk in a dust mask weighs flour, levels the scoop with a steel ruler, and writes a number on the back of a child's hand. The line does not push. Pushing cost a day, once, and the line remembers.

phases.name: ESTABLISHING THE RUN (DAYS 1-4)
phases.lead: The first four serials set every pattern the next ten inherit: route discipline, identification checks, queue layout, and the warden relationship. The cell watches the first runs and plans against them — assume day one is being graded.

routes.name: Corridor KALE
routes.desc: 9.8 km through the glass belt, three mapped hot spots, transit dose-budgeted at {DOSE_TRANSITS} crossings per crew per week.
routes.tradeoff: Two serials a day inside the cold-chain window — paid for in crew dose, with any halt past 18 minutes in a hot zone counting double.

routes.name: Corridor MILLET
routes.desc: 22.4 km, radiologically cold, two collapsed-underpass chokepoints where one stalled truck stops the serial dead.
routes.tradeoff: No dose ledger and one serial a day — the 21-day window spent to nearly nothing, and both chokepoints are ambush ground either side can read.

dataBlock.Cold chain: 21 days from landing date, refrigerated antibiotics
dataBlock.Comms blackout: 40 percent of both corridors — pre-planned schedules substitute for radio
dataBlock.Attack pattern: every third day plus or minus one; five attacks in fifteen days

phases.name: THE GRIND (DAYS 5-18)
phases.lead: The middle two weeks are the contract: the same run, fourteen times, against a cell that needs to be right once. Variation is deliberate, fatigue is managed on a roster, and the pattern day — every third day, plus or minus one — is planned for by name.

protocol.Serial authentication: day codeword pairs issued to the warden net at 0500; a truck answering yesterday's word is stopped at 200 m as a forgery
protocol.Handoff receipt: the warden counter-signs the tonnage slip at transfer; no signature, no transfer — the audit clause reads slips, not memories
protocol.Mortar drill: on first impact the barriers open OUTWARD on the marshal's whistle — the surge kills at the barriers, not at the impact point

sidebarKernel.kernel: Two ledgers run side by side: dosimeters and reefer temperatures. Both are written in numbers nobody can argue with afterward, and both are read every night — the crew that exceeds its dose and the antibiotic that breaks its chain fail the same way: quietly, two weeks later.

phases.name: CLOSE-OUT (DAYS 19-21)
phases.lead: The last serials move when the cold-chain margin is already spent and the cell knows the schedule as well as the dispatcher does. The final three days run at full escort discipline — the contract's record is set by its last day, not its best one.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The handover that outlives the invoice is the distribution system itself: if the wardens can run day 22 without an escort, the bonus clause is met and so is the point.

assetDetails.detail: Heads the district warden arrangement. Can move a serial's tonnage to households in 6 hours where the consortium plan needs 14 — at an 8 to 15 percent skim that is itself the wardens' payroll. Deals straight if dealt with straight, and never inside a running vehicle: meetings happen standing, in the open, where the district can see them.

The antibiotic reefers hold temperature 11 hours unpowered; each needs 4 hours of generator time daily. A reefer stalled in a comms blackout zone past its power window is a cargo loss that never shows a bullet hole — the recovery plan is a logistics order, not a rescue.

comstar.situation.framing: {TARGET_FACTION}'s broadcasts call the orbital attack a cleansing and the queues a penance. Refuse the vocabulary. What burned here was an archive of the living, and what remains is a congregation of ration cards. The relief column is the only liturgy this city has left that means what it says: bread, weighed honestly, at the appointed hour. See that the hour is kept.

DOSE_TRANSITS.unit: KALE transits per crew per week
