title: OPERATION GREY PSALM
skeleton: rescue team must extract a fixed list of people ahead of a purge while one name on the list belongs to an informer no analysis can identify in advance
inspiration: clandestine extraction of marked persons ahead of a roundup (e.g. escape-line exfiltrations of listed individuals, 1943)
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The compound on the hill has broadcast the evening Vigil for two hundred years. It still does. The words have not changed; what the words are being used for has. Since {TARGET_FACTION} took custody of the local HPG, the station staff have been going through what the occupiers call reconsecration screening: interviews, then lists. People on the first list go back to their duties. People on the second list are reassigned within the compound. People on the third list are transferred off-site, and no transfer has yet been followed by a letter, a sighting, or a name spoken aloud. The next third list is read on the 14th of the month — {SCREENING_DAYS} days from the date of this briefing. {EMPLOYER} needs nine of those names out and elsewhere before the list is read, along with two cipher cores from the transmission vault, {CORE_MASS} kilograms each.

The nine, by role: two transmission engineers, one cryptography adept, three maintenance specialists, one records clerk, two dependents. Screening schedules and interior layouts come from {NPC:intel-source}, placed inside the compound's laundry contract; that intelligence is six days old and fairly solid. One more item, for command eyes only: handler analysis believes one of the nine is already reporting to {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence. That rests on meeting-interval patterns alone, so it is a suspicion, not proof. Do not try to work out which one in the field. The decision annex covers what you may do about it; improvising does not.

The terrain problem is the reservoir stairs: nine terraced reservoirs descending 310 meters from the compound hill to the valley floor, crossable only along the dam crests. Crests 1 and 6 are rated to carry BattleMech weight. Every sluice gate in the system is controlled remotely from the compound, and the duty engineer can put 1.8 meters of fast-moving water over any crest with 90 seconds' notice. The enemy does not need to shoot you off the stairs. It only needs to open a valve.

Garrison: one {TARGET_FACTION} Level II — six units, a mix of BattleMechs and battle armor, C3i-networked — barracked 700 meters from the main gate, plus a local militia infantry company, plus an informant network in the valley towns dense enough that any contact with a civilian should be assumed to reach militia ears within 2 to 6 hours. The Vigil broadcast doubles as the district public-address system, so a lockdown order travels at the speed of a hymn. Time your movements to the religious offices the hill still keeps. It will be singing while you work.

objectives.primary: Extract the nine listed personnel and both cipher cores before the third list is read, and deliver them to the pickup point intact.
objectives.secondary: Preserve {NPC:intel-source}'s placement: no action that identifies the laundry contract as the leak.
objectives.bonus: Cut or corrupt the compound's sluice-control lines at the No. 4 valve house during egress, leaving the reservoir stairs crossable for whoever comes next.

complications.name: The Valves
complications.text: Sluice control runs from the compound. Any crest crossing can be put under 1.8 meters of moving water on 90 seconds' notice, and the duty engineer drills the procedure weekly. Water does not miss.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From T+7:00, any unit on a crest hex risks flooding each turn: infantry swept (casualty checks), BattleMechs make piloting checks at penalty. Cutting the control lines at the No. 4 valve house (engineering action, 2 turns) disables the hazard permanently.

complications.name: C3i Level II
complications.text: Six machines sharing one set of eyes. The first contact report any of them makes is a firing solution for all of them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The Level II fights with networked targeting (improved to-hit while linked). Destroying or jamming the network node breaks the link; until then, engaging one means being ranged by six.

complications.name: The Hymn Is a Siren
complications.text: The Vigil channel reaches every receiver in the district. A lockdown order interrupts the broadcast and puts the militia on the streets with checkpoint orders inside minutes.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the compound issues a lockdown, the militia reaction timeline advances by one full step and all civilian-area movement requires evasion checks.

complications.name: Fragile Cargo
complications.text: The cipher cores do not tolerate electromagnetic shock. A core riding in a machine that takes PPC fire is a brick with a history.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each core is carried by a designated unit. Energy-weapon hits on the carrier roll for core integrity; a destroyed core halves the success grading of the mission.

decisionPoints.name: When
decisionPoints.context: The compound runs on a schedule of religious services, and each service opens a different opportunity to move.

options.title: During the Vigil (1930-2010)
advantages: Guard posts at devotional minimum manning — the lowest sentry density of any 24-hour period
The broadcast masks low-frequency noise across the hill
The nine know the office schedule as well as the guards do; coordination windows are natural
disadvantages: Curfew empties the streets: anything moving in the valley towns is anomalous by definition
The Vigil channel is live in every receiver — the lockdown order travels instantly if triggered
Forty minutes, not one more; the office ends and the posts re-man
options.consequence: The quietest door and the loudest alarm behind it. Everything must fit inside the hymn.

costs.resource: window: 40 minutes, not one more — every phase sized to fit inside the hymn
costs.risk: curfew streets: anything moving in the valley towns is anomalous by definition

options.title: Shift Change at 0600
advantages: Maximum bodies in motion: the gate queue, the screening lines, the laundry vans — nine more people moving is noise in the noise
Biometric turnstiles process slowly; queue chaos is institutional, expected, and exploitable
Daylight movement in the valley reads as commerce, not infiltration
disadvantages: Full garrison awake and at posts; the Level II stands its morning readiness check at 0615
The turnstiles are still turnstiles: each of the nine must defeat one, and one failure flags the gate
Crowds cut both ways — a crowd is concealment until it is a witness pool
options.consequence: Hiding inside the routine. The plan inherits every virtue of the morning and the Level II at its most awake.

costs.resource: forged credentials: nine turnstile-grade identities, expended whether they pass or fail
costs.risk: the Level II stands its readiness check at 0615 — the full garrison awake at your worst minute

options.title: False Radiological Alarm
advantages: The compound's own evacuation plan empties it: the nine walk out inside a procedure the guards themselves enforce
Captured {TARGET_FACTION} protocol codes make the alarm internally credible for 60 to 90 minutes
No turnstiles, no curfew problem — the crowd is ordered into the open by its own commanders
disadvantages: The codes burn forever: one use, and every captured protocol in the employer's inventory is suspect afterward
The after-action sweep will be total — screening restarts from zero, harder, for everyone left behind
If the deception is read in real time, the compound locks down with the nine inside and the garrison pre-alerted
options.consequence: The cleanest extraction available, paid for with a strategic asset and a compound full of people who will answer for it after you are gone.

costs.resource: captured {TARGET_FACTION} protocol codes: burned forever on first use — every captured protocol in the employer's inventory suspect afterward
costs.risk: a deception read in real time locks the compound down with the nine inside and the garrison pre-alerted

decisionPoints.name: The Ninth Name
decisionPoints.context: Pattern-analysis says one of the nine reports to {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence. The analysis cannot say which. The plan must say what happens anyway.

options.title: Bring All Nine as Planned
advantages: No tribunal conducted in a stairwell on statistical evidence
The extraction proceeds at full speed with no separation overhead
If the analysis is wrong, no innocent person was left to the third list on arithmetic
disadvantages: The risk travels with you: route, timing, and pickup point are all observable by whoever it is
Enemy counterintelligence may already hold the pickup coordinates if the report interval allows one more meeting
options.consequence: The whole problem is deferred to the destination, where the employer's counterintelligence does its work properly — if the column lives that long.

costs.risk: route, timing, and pickup observable from inside the column — the wager is the column itself

options.title: Leave the Suspect Profile Behind
advantages: The route stays clean; whatever the enemy gets, it does not get from inside the column
Eight extracted with certainty beats nine extracted on a wager
disadvantages: The analysis is interval mathematics, not proof — the person left may be ordinary and loyal and doomed
The roles are not interchangeable: losing the cryptography adept or both engineers degrades the strategic objective
Whoever is left behind goes to the third list knowing roughly why
options.consequence: A possibly innocent name stays on the hill, and the column carries that arithmetic home along with the cores. Count it. It does not get smaller later.

costs.resource: one of nine names left to the third list on interval mathematics — possibly the cryptography adept the objective needs
costs.risk: if the roles fall wrong, the strategic objective degrades by exactly the person left on the hill

options.title: Separate Transport for the Suspect Profile
advantages: The main column's route and pickup stay compartmented from the highest-risk passenger
All nine extracted; the strategic objective intact regardless of which way the analysis falls
disadvantages: A second route means a second escort, a second pickup, and double the exposure surface
The separated party is weakly protected by definition — if the enemy moves, it moves on them first
The suspect will understand what the separation means; so will the other eight
options.consequence: Everyone leaves and nobody is trusted. The two columns spend the night proving the handler's suspicion was survivable, one checkpoint at a time.

costs.resource: a second escort, a second route, a second pickup: the exposure surface doubled for one passenger
costs.risk: the separated party is weakly protected by design — if the enemy moves, it moves on them first

entries.event: Compound alarm: sentry contact, turnstile flag, or deception read in real time.
Lockdown order on the Vigil/public-address channel; valley militia begins moving to checkpoints.
Level II reaction element moving — barracks to main gate is 700 meters.
Sluice authority passes to the duty engineer; crest flooding available on 90 seconds' notice.
Crests 1 and 6 under fire, under water, or both. The Stairs close.
Militia checkpoint net complete across the valley towns; {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence mobile teams begin sweep interviews.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Across the reservoir stairs not later than T+11:00. After that, the valley-floor route adds 9 kilometers under C3i overwatch, and the pickup point holds until 0140 and not one minute past — the next window is in four days, and the third list is read in {SCREENING_DAYS}.

opforSketch.composition: One {TARGET_FACTION} Level II: six units, mixed BattleMech and battle armor, C3i-networked (Veteran, treat as Elite while the network holds). One local militia infantry company (Regular) distributed across valley checkpoints. {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence mobile teams (Veteran) active within 25 minutes of lockdown. Generator should keep the Level II as a single coherent threat, not dispersed pickets.
opforSketch.behavior: Lockdown-first doctrine: the compound secures people and lists before it pursues intruders. Uses water, checkpoints, and the public-address channel as weapons ahead of lasers. The Level II pursues methodically under network discipline and will not be baited into breaking C3i cohesion. The enemy counterintelligence interest outlives the night.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAR CHANNEL
forks.trigger: Nine extracted, both cores intact, source placement preserved.
forks.consequence: The cores break local {TARGET_FACTION} traffic inside three weeks. Sector convoys reroute around three ambushes that never happen, and a follow-on raid is offered with the occupier's patrol grid decrypted in advance — the rarest commodity of the war: foreknowledge.

forks.name: OPERATION THIRD LIST
forks.trigger: Extraction aborted or defeated; the screening proceeds.
forks.consequence: The lists are read on schedule. The laundry-contract source goes silent within a week. {EMPLOYER} orders a second attempt — heavier, louder, against an alerted compound — because the cores' value survives everything except the vault being moved, and the vault is being moved.

forks.name: OPERATION WHITE NOISE
forks.trigger: The attempt is traced to the valley network, regardless of extraction outcome.
forks.consequence: {TARGET_FACTION} reprisal screenings begin in the towns within 72 hours. Every asset the employer holds in the valley must be exfiltrated inside that window — a second extraction, unplanned, with the first one's pursuit still in the air.

storyElementSeed: Evening. The hill sings the same office it has sung for two hundred years, on key, on time. Below the dam, a technician checks a watch against the third verse and starts walking.

phases.name: PHASE I — THE APPROACH
phases.lead: The element crosses the reservoir stairs inbound and is in position before the chosen office begins: every crest crossing logged against the sluice problem, every halt sited off the dam crests, and the laundry-contract source untouched — her information arrives by drop, never by meeting.

dataBlock.Reservoir stairs: nine terraced reservoirs descending 310 m; crossings along dam crests only
dataBlock.Rated crests: crests 1 and 6 carry BattleMech mass; all others infantry-only
dataBlock.Sluice hazard: any crest under 1.8 m of moving water on 90 seconds' notice, controlled from the compound
dataBlock.Garrison: {TARGET_FACTION} Level II (6 units, C3i) barracked 700 m from the main gate; militia company across the valley towns
dataBlock.Informant latency: any civilian contact in the valley reaches militia ears within 2 to 6 hours

phases.name: PHASE II — THE GATHERING
phases.lead: The nine are collected inside the window the timing decision bought, in an order set by role: the cryptography adept and both engineers move first with the core-carry party, the dependents move with escort, and nobody is told more of the route than the leg they are walking. The vault work runs parallel — two cores, {CORE_MASS} kilograms each, hand-carried, never on the same vehicle.

protocol.Recognition: the contact phrase is the second line of the evening psalter, answered with the fifth — wrong verse, walk on
protocol.Assembly signal: a maintenance lantern in the No. 2 pump house window, lit at the office's first versicle, out at the last
protocol.Source protection: no member of the element approaches the laundry route, its vans, or its schedule — a burned drop is an abort, not a problem to solve
protocol.Abort word: TENEBRAE, spoken or transmitted in clear: scatter to hide sites and hold 48 hours

sidebarKernel.kernel: One of the nine reports to {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence and the analysis cannot say which. Field rule: nobody learns the pickup point until they are standing on it. Curiosity about the route is data — log who asks, and do not act on it.

phases.name: PHASE III — THE STAIRS
phases.lead: Egress is a race between the column and the duty engineer's valves: across the rated crests not later than T+11:00, with the No. 4 valve house action run by the engineering party while the crossings are still dry. The pickup holds until 0140 and not one minute past.

routes.name: Route VERSICLE — Crest 1
routes.desc: The upper rated crossing: 400 m of dam crest directly below the compound wall, then the short descent to the valley road.
routes.tradeoff: Shortest path to the pickup by 3.1 km — and the first crest the duty engineer floods when the lockdown order interrupts the hymn.

routes.name: Route RESPONSE — Crest 6
routes.desc: The lower rated crossing, reached by the maintenance switchbacks past the No. 4 valve house.
routes.tradeoff: Adds 40 minutes at dependent pace, at night — and passes the one point on the stairs where the flood hazard can be cut for good.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The No. 4 valve house is a 2-turn job: cut the control runs, leave the local hand-wheels — the valley needs its irrigation even if the occupier does not deserve its weapon. Done right, the stairs stay a bridge. Done loud, they stay a trap with your crossing time in the logbook.

assetDetails.detail: Two transmission engineers, one cryptography adept, three maintenance specialists, one records clerk, two dependents. The clerk's screening interview is scheduled 2 days before the third list is read — if the operation slips, the clerk is questioned first. One dependent is 71 years old and cannot manage the crest stairs at column pace: powered transport, or a 25-minute penalty on every Stairs leg.

Placed inside the compound's laundry contract and staying behind — placement survival is the secondary objective. Information moves one way, by drop, on the laundry van schedule; the source has never met the element and never will. Any plan that needs a question answered mid-operation is a plan that burns the source.

{CORE_MASS} kg each, intolerant of electromagnetic shock: never on the same vehicle, never on a carrier inside the C3i engagement envelope while the network link holds. The carry assignment is written into the order of march, with a designated alternate per core.

merc.situation.framing: The employer calls it reconsecration screening. Read annex C: it is a purge with paperwork, and the bonus clause for all nine alive is priced the way it is because the employer knows exactly what the third list means. Mind the dams — the force majeure language in this contract does not mention drowning, and that omission was not accidental either.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Separate Transport for the Suspect Profile
resourceGates.lackingText: No second lift exists: separation holds only on the ground route, and both parties converge on the single employer pickup at 0140 — the compartmentation buys the road, not the ride.

title: OPERATION DRY SEASON
skeleton: garrison must keep two of three dispersed utilities alive with a force that cannot hold all three while the attacker reads which one was abandoned and a sabotage clock punishes every outage
inspiration: defense of dispersed waterworks against raiders (e.g. infrastructure protection in a colonial counter-insurgency)
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The capital draws its water from below and pumps it up. The upper city sits above the scarp, a 90-meter cliff that splits the capital in two, and holds 610,000 people. Three lift stations pump water up to it from the wadi galleries below. The cisterns up top hold only 36 hours' worth at ration levels. {TARGET_FACTION} raiders have probed the lifts three times in five weeks. They work from a coastal hideout whose location is unconfirmed, based only on two intercepted boat transponders that are nine days old. The last raid knocked out Lift 2 for 19 hours, and the upper city learned exactly what 19 hours costs: ration lines at the standpipes, two nights of curfew, and a black market in water cans the constabulary has stopped policing. {EMPLOYER} has tasked your command with garrisoning the lift stations. Your orders carry two countersignatures, because the provincial assembly's defence committee and the province's military liaison ({NPC:employer-contact}) disagree about whose signature you actually need, and each has put that in writing. Both letters are in your annex. Read them once, then go defend the water.

Your force is whatever the year leaves you. One BattleMech lance: three machines running, the fourth waiting on a gyro aboard a DropShip that has been '8 days out' for three weeks now, so treat that promise as unreliable. Two militia armor platoons: eight Vedettes on paper, but only {RUNNING_VEDETTES} actually running on a given morning. {CONSCRIPTS} conscript infantry with 11 days of training. Two agricultural VTOLs fitted with rocket pods: one sortie per airframe per day, no night flying. Munitions stand at {AMMO_ESTABLISHMENT} percent of establishment. This is the combined-arms problem at its harshest: no elegance, just arithmetic.

The terrain problem is the scarp itself. The lifts cling to a vertical cliff face, and the only approaches are a switchback road (armor-passable, but observed end to end), the old funicular cut (infantry only), and the crest line, exposed to anything out in the bay. You are defending three points on a cliff wall with a force built to fight in open country. The raiders know the geography — their demolition teams reached a lift perimeter within 12 minutes in two of three attempts. The pattern says they are rehearsing for one big raid meant to knock out all three lifts at once. The cisterns hold 36 hours. The assembly debates. The water table does neither.

objectives.primary: Keep a minimum of two of three lift stations pumping at all times across the 60-day garrison period; no outage of any lift to exceed 36 hours.
objectives.secondary: Fix the coastal hide: confirmed location and composition of the raiding force, delivered to provincial command with evidence sufficient to act on.
objectives.bonus: End the period with the conscript battalion certified for independent lift defense — the garrison that does not need you is the one the province can afford.

complications.name: Eleven Days of Training
complications.text: The conscripts hold positions adequately and patrol acceptably and have never once been under indirect fire. The first mortar round will teach whatever the cadre failed to.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Conscript units under indirect fire make morale checks; failure is grounded cowering, not rout. Cadre or BattleMech presence within 2 hexes negates the check.

complications.name: Hands in the Machinery
complications.text: After a 'maintenance' visit, Lift 1's surge-tank valve was found re-set to a failure position. The repair crews are local, necessary, and unvetted — and vetting them slows every repair the lifts need.
complications.mechanicalEffect: An active sabotage clock runs unless crew vetting is instituted; vetting adds 20 percent to all repair times. Unvetted crews roll for a sabotage event after each major maintenance action.

complications.name: The Countersignature Problem
complications.text: Operations beyond the city boundary require defence-committee countersignature: 48 hours, minimum, in practice. The provincial liaison says otherwise. The paperwork war has its own front line, and it moves slower than the real one.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Out-of-boundary operations are delayed 48 hours unless the relevant decision-point option is taken. Acting without countersignature succeeds operationally but advances a political-standing track against the unit.

complications.name: Forty Percent of Establishment
complications.text: Rocket pods, SRM reloads, and autocannon bins are at {AMMO_ESTABLISHMENT} percent. The resupply DropShip remains '8 days out.' Every engagement is also a withdrawal from an account that is not refilling.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track ammunition across engagements. Below 20 percent of establishment, weapon-use restrictions apply (no speculative or suppressive fire); the resupply arrival is a campaign roll, not a promise.

decisionPoints.name: Three Lifts, Two Platoons
decisionPoints.context: The math of the scarp will not give you three strong garrisons from this force. What it gives you instead is a choice about where to be weak.

options.title: Hold All Three, Thin
advantages: No lift conceded; no district told it matters less
The political settlement — committee and province both — stays intact
Raiders must still rehearse three problems, not two
disadvantages: Every garrison is under the strength the last raid already beat
The mobile reserve is one understrength lance for a 9-kilometer frontage on a wall
A simultaneous two-lift raid wins against this layout on paper, and they have the paper
options.consequence: Equity as a defensive doctrine. Nothing is abandoned and nothing is strong, and the raiders' rehearsals continue against a known, divided layout.

costs.resource: mobile reserve: one understrength lance covering 9 kilometers of wall
costs.risk: a simultaneous two-lift raid beats this layout on paper, and the rehearsals say they have the paper

options.title: Concede Lift 2, Hold 1 and 3 Strong
advantages: Two genuinely defensible garrisons instead of three notional ones
Repair stocks pre-positioned at Lift 2 turn its outages from crises into schedules
The lance concentrates instead of commuting
disadvantages: The 19-hour lesson becomes policy: the districts fed by Lift 2 are told, in effect, to keep jerry cans
The Committee will read concession as dereliction, in writing, with copies
The raiders get a free rehearsal target and the initiative that comes with it
options.consequence: Military honesty at political cost. The water ledger improves; the standing-track and the standpipe queues at District 2 keep their own books.

costs.resource: political standing: the Committee files the concession as dereliction, in writing, with copies
costs.risk: District 2 keeps jerry cans and a grievance — the 19-hour lesson made policy

options.title: Strip the Lifts and Strike the Hide
advantages: The only option that ends the raids instead of surviving them
The VTOLs and the boat-transponder intercepts give a real, if thin, targeting start
A destroyed hide returns the whole garrison problem to ordinary watchkeeping
disadvantages: The lifts stand at skeleton strength for 36 hours; if the strike misses, the city has no real margin left
Out-of-boundary, so the countersignature problem is at its worst: act and answer for it, or wait 48 hours and give the move away
The hide's location rests on two transponder hits, nine days old — a weak, unconfirmed fix
options.consequence: The garrison bets its whole purpose on thin intelligence. Right, and the dry season ends early. Wrong, and the raiders find three lifts held by conscripts and a written record of who ordered the wall emptied.

costs.resource: munitions: an estimated 10-15 points of establishment spent on the strike, from stocks already below half
costs.risk: 36 hours of skeleton-strength lifts, staked on a weak fix: two transponder hits, nine days old

decisionPoints.name: The VTOL Question
decisionPoints.context: Two crop-dusters with rocket pods are your entire air force. You can spend them on finding the enemy, saving wounded, or watching the approaches — once per day, in daylight only.

options.title: Armed Reconnaissance Over the Bay
advantages: The only organic means of fixing the coastal hide
Rocket pods make a found target a serviced target, once
disadvantages: The raiders carry shoulder-launched SAMs (observed at raid 2); a downed crop-duster is a dead crew and half the air force
Registered agricultural airframes flying armed recon forfeit whatever civil protection the registry pretended to give them
options.consequence: The air force becomes a reconnaissance asset with a life expectancy. The hide gets found, or the search dies trying, and either way the answer arrives this month.

costs.resource: one airframe and crew exposed per sortie, one sortie per day — half the air force per SAM event
costs.risk: a downed crop-duster is a dead crew, and the agricultural registry protection is forfeited on the first armed sortie

options.title: Reserve for Casualty Evacuation
advantages: A guaranteed medevac lift halves died-of-wounds among conscripts who will absorb the first raid badly
The promise of evacuation measurably steadies green troops — morale arithmetic, not sentiment
disadvantages: The hide stays unfixed; the strategic question stays open
Two airframes idle through every quiet day of the garrison period
options.consequence: The air force becomes an insurance policy. The conscripts fight better and the raiders' base remains a rumor with boat engines.

costs.resource: the coastal hide stays unfixed: the strategic question stands open for the full 60 days
costs.risk: two airframes idle through every quiet day — the cost is paid in initiative, not airframes

options.title: Night Static Posts on the Crest
advantages: Crews dismounted with optics turn the airframes' sensors into a fixed early-warning line
No flight exposure: the SAM question never gets asked
Raid warning moves from 'pickets at the breakwater' to 'boats on the bay' — 15 added minutes
disadvantages: The airframes themselves sit parked and targetable behind the crest
Neither evacuation nor reconnaissance is available without unwinding the arrangement first
options.consequence: The air force becomes a pair of expensive binoculars. The warning margin grows; the options list shrinks to what the ground force can do with the extra quarter hour.

costs.resource: air options forfeited: neither medevac nor reconnaissance without unwinding the arrangement first
costs.risk: parked airframes behind the crest are targets that cannot dodge

entries.event: Picket contact: boats at the breakwater or movement on the bay road.
Mortar fire on lift approaches begins; conscript morale checks start here.
Raider fast movers (hover and wheeled) reach the switchback base.
Demolition teams at a lift perimeter — observed twice in three prior raids.
Garrison armor platoon on scene if the switchback is clear; later if it is mined, and it has been mined.
Demolition teams set charges regardless of their own casualties; raid elements begin withdrawal to the bay.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Any demolition team on a lift platform past T+25:00 will fire its charges. From that moment the 36-hour cistern clock runs: lift restored inside 36 hours or the upper city's taps go dry — and a city that has already counted 19 hours knows exactly how long 36 is.

opforSketch.composition: {TARGET_FACTION} raiding force, boat-inserted: fast hover and wheeled elements (Regular), demolition teams (Veteran), one mortar section, shoulder-launched SAMs confirmed. Possible light fire support from the bay (UNCONFIRMED). No BattleMechs observed to date; generator may introduce one Level I of machines only at the campaign's climax raid.
opforSketch.behavior: Rehearsal doctrine: each raid tests one approach and withdraws before decisive contact. Mines the switchback behind itself, targets infrastructure over personnel, and avoids attrition it cannot replace. The climax raid — all three lifts at once — comes only after the rehearsals stop showing them anything new.

forks.name: OPERATION WET SEASON
forks.trigger: Lifts held through the period and the coastal hide fixed or destroyed.
forks.consequence: Provincial command lands a proper armor company and takes the scarp off your books. The unit is offered the counter-raid along the coast — same enemy, better odds, and this time the intelligence is yours.

forks.name: OPERATION HIGH GROUND EMPTY
forks.trigger: Any lift down beyond 36 hours, or two lifts down simultaneously.
forks.consequence: The upper city begins moving downhill — 610,000 people, 36 hours of water, one switchback road. The garrison's final tasking is route security for a descending city while {TARGET_FACTION} broadcasts narrate the failure to three neighboring systems.

forks.name: OPERATION PATCHWORK
forks.trigger: Lifts held but munitions exhausted below 20 percent of establishment.
forks.consequence: The garrison passes to static defense only: no patrols, no spoiling attacks, no answer to the next rehearsal except sandbags and morale checks. Everything now waits on a DropShip that has been '8 days out' since anyone can remember.

storyElementSeed: On the crest at dusk, a conscript counts tracer intervals under his breath the way the cadre taught — one-and-two-and — and writes the bearing on the sandbag in chalk, because paper blows away up here.

phases.name: POSTURE (DAYS 1-14)
phases.lead: The first two weeks set the garrison the raiders will rehearse against: the lift-allocation decision executed and documented, repair-crew vetting begun, and the conscripts drilled on the one thing eleven days of training did not teach — staying in a hole while mortar rounds land. Both patron letters are answered in writing; neither is answered first.

dataBlock.Lift stations: 3, clinging to the 90 m scarp; cisterns above hold 36 hours at ration
dataBlock.Approaches: switchback road (armor-passable, observed end to end), funicular cut (infantry only), crest line (exposed to the bay)
dataBlock.Raid pattern: 3 probes in 5 weeks; demolition teams reached a lift perimeter inside 12 minutes in 2 of 3
dataBlock.Munitions: {AMMO_ESTABLISHMENT} percent of establishment; resupply '8 days out' for 3 weeks
dataBlock.Air: 2 agricultural VTOLs, one sortie per airframe per day, no night operations

phases.name: THE REHEARSALS
phases.lead: Each probe is mutual instruction: they test one approach and withdraw; the garrison logs timings, mends wire, and resists the urge to spend ammunition reassuring itself. Every engagement is read against the establishment ledger before it is praised.

protocol.Raid alert: codeword DRY WELL on the garrison net puts all three lifts to stand-to and starts the reaction clock
protocol.Landline discipline: lift stations report by buried landline on the quarter hour during alerts; a missed report is treated as contact, not as a fault
protocol.Out-of-boundary rule: pursuit beyond the city boundary requires defence-committee countersignature unless the duty log records 'forces in contact' — write the log entry first, argue the signatures after
protocol.Medevac: if the VTOLs are held for evacuation, code LITTER BEAR tasks one airframe; daylight only, and the crews know it

sidebarKernel.kernel: The ledger stands at {AMMO_ESTABLISHMENT} percent and the DropShip has been '8 days out' for three weeks. Every fire mission is a withdrawal from an account nobody is refilling — sign for each one as if the Committee will audit it, because it will.

phases.name: THE CLIMAX RAID
phases.lead: The rehearsals end when they stop showing the raiders anything new; the real raid comes for all three lifts at once, and the garrison's answer is the layout chosen in week one plus whatever the conscripts have become since. From the first charge fired, the 36-hour cistern clock is the only schedule that matters — repair priority is set by water arithmetic, not by which district writes to the assembly first.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The conscripts' first indirect fire fills the aid post with concussion and panic in equal measure — triage the panic too, visibly, and the second hour goes better than the first. Died-of-wounds halves when the evacuation promise is kept the one time it is tested.

assetDetails.detail: Three crews, 26 tradesmen, unvetted and irreplaceable — no lift restarts inside 36 hours without them. After Lift 1's surge-tank valve was found re-set to a failure position, the choice is explicit: vet them and add 20 percent to every repair, or work them unvetted and roll for sabotage after each major maintenance action. Split the difference and the garrison pays both costs.

The provincial liaison: will countersign anything retroactively if the duty log is clean, and nothing prospectively while the committee dispute stands. Send the liaison the same daily summary the committee receives, unedited — the day the two patrons compare documents is the day the unit's paper either saves it or hangs it.

merc.situation.framing: Two signatures, two patrons, one chain of command on paper and none in practice. Get the precedence question settled in writing before the first raid, not during it — an order you cannot trace is an invoice nobody pays. The water is the mission; the committee is the weather.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Strip the Lifts and Strike the Hide
resourceGates.lackingText: No lift for the strike force: the approach goes overland down the coast road, and the lifts stand at skeleton strength for 60 hours instead of 36 — the brief prints the longer window.

title: OPERATION DEAD LETTER
skeleton: hunter must corner and finish a raider's escape lift inside a single predicted window while the local infrastructure of betrayal that feeds the raiders sits outside the contract entirely
inspiration: anti-piracy patrols against raiders who beat pursuit to sea (e.g. counter-corsair sweeps timed to a raider's tide window)
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. This world's HPG went dark with all the rest years ago. The mail packet calls every {PACKET_CYCLE} days; help is two jumps and a month away in a good month; and the people who figured that out fastest were not the planetary government's planners. A raider group the grain co-ops call the Tallow Jacks has hit the terminal grain elevators three times in five months, each strike timed to the window right after the packet sails — when {WORLD} cannot get word out to anyone for nearly four weeks. They fly scrubbed transponders that answer military challenge codes two years out of date, and with the registry network down there is no live database to catch the lie; the militia's anti-air battery has already holed the mail packet's own shuttle once on a bad call. The communications blackout is not just background here. It is the terrain the enemy maneuvers in.

The physical terrain problem is the salt hardpan: a salt flat 70 kilometers from the terminals, hard as ferrocrete, with no cover on the approach for 11 kilometers in any direction. The Jacks land one mixed-bay DropShip there and run loot convoys to the terminals and back. Across three raids they stayed on the ground 6 hours 40 minutes, 7 hours 10 minutes, and 6 hours 55 minutes; those figures are 41 days old, so treat them as a guide, not a guarantee. They lift off before anything can reach them, because anything coming for them is visible for an hour before it arrives. On the last raid they took {HOSTAGES} co-op workers. A released hostage says they are held aboard the ship as labor, but that is one account, 38 days old, and unconfirmed.

{EMPLOYER} — the planetary legislature's emergency commission, through {NPC:employer-contact} — has contracted your unit to end the raids, with a bonus schedule keyed to the number of hostages recovered alive. Supporting assets: two militia armor companies, high on enthusiasm and short on gunnery; a spotter network of co-op silo watchers on hand-cranked field telephones, because the blackout forces old solutions; and no aerospace of any kind.

One more thread. An amateur astronomer logged a drive flare on a bearing that lines up with a nonstandard jump point. It is a single uncalibrated sighting, so it is unconfirmed, but it fits. Somebody is recharging the Jacks' JumpShip. Somebody schedules these raids around the packet cycle, which means somebody is reading the packet schedule. The contract is for the DropShip. The decision annex is for the bigger question behind it.

objectives.primary: End the Tallow Jacks' raiding capability on {WORLD}: destroy, capture, or permanently deter the DropShip and its ground element.
objectives.secondary: Recover the {HOSTAGES} co-op hostages alive — the bonus schedule is keyed per head, and so is the town that is waiting.
objectives.bonus: Recover the DropShip's navigation core or equivalent records fixing the renegade JumpShip's recharge point.

complications.name: Stale Codes, Live Guns
complications.text: The Jacks squawk old military transponder codes that were valid two years ago, and nothing on {WORLD} can prove otherwise in real time. The militia's worst engagement to date was nearly against the mail shuttle.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All unidentified contacts squawk friendly until visually identified inside 500 meters. Engagement before visual identification risks a blue-on-blue event; militia units roll fire-discipline checks against ambiguous contacts.

complications.name: Hostages Aboard
complications.text: The released hostage's count puts the co-op workers on the DropShip itself, used as cargo handlers. Every plan that ends with the ship burning ends with them inside it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Area-effect and capital-scale fire against the DropShip is restricted while hostages are believed aboard; the bonus objective requires a boarding or surrender outcome, not a kill.

complications.name: Green Companies
complications.text: The militia armor companies will charge anything you point them at, which is the problem. Their gunnery is green and their radios are older than their crews.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Militia units act on simple orders only (one clause, no conditionals) and roll fire-discipline checks on first contact. They count double for screening and crowd-presence tasks.

complications.name: The 27-Day Economics
complications.text: The raid window opens when the packet sails. If the Jacks skip a cycle — and they have once — the contract idles at day-rate against a planet that budgets in harvests.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If the strike window passes without a raid, the employer invokes renegotiation: reduced retainer, success bonus intact. The unit's posture decision (dispersed wait vs. concentrated readiness) carries a real cost either way.

decisionPoints.name: Where to Meet Them
decisionPoints.context: The hardpan is theirs, the terminals are yours, and the 70 kilometers of road between them is where you decide how to fight.

options.title: Dig In at the Terminals
advantages: Defends the actual prize: the elevators, the co-op, the people
Militia fights best from prepared positions with simple sectors
No reliance on a 41-day-old pattern holding
disadvantages: Surrenders the Hardpan and the initiative: the ship grounds, loads, and lifts unmolested if it picks a different target
The Jacks have raided two other co-ops 200 kilometers up the line before; fixed defense defends one address
Zero progress toward the hostages or the nav core
options.consequence: The safe play. The elevators survive, the raids continue, and the contract's success clauses sit unclaimed on the table.

costs.resource: initiative: the Hardpan, the hostages, and the raid schedule stay theirs
costs.risk: fixed defense defends one address — the Jacks have raided co-ops 200 kilometers up the line before

options.title: Hide on the Hardpan Approaches
advantages: The only plan that catches the DropShip on the ground, where it is a building instead of a spacecraft
Thermal blinds and dug-in positions beat the 11-kilometer visibility problem — if emplaced before the ship grounds
Boarding becomes possible: hostages and nav core both live inside this option
disadvantages: Commits everything to a 41-day-old pattern and a guess about the grounding spot; the flat is big and the pattern is three data points
Days of concealed waiting in salt glare with water hauled in by night
If they ground 20 kilometers off the guess, the force is a garrison of nowhere
options.consequence: The decisive option, balanced on a pattern analysis. Right, and the whole problem ends in one afternoon. Wrong, and the raid happens on the news while the unit eats salt.

costs.resource: water and thermal discipline: every liter hauled in by night for the whole concealed wait
costs.risk: a 41-day-old three-point pattern — ground 20 kilometers off the guess and the force is a garrison of nowhere

options.title: Ambush the Loot Convoy at the Cut
advantages: The Cut is the only defile on the terminal road: real ambush ground with cover and exits
Destroys the raid's economics without betting on the grounding spot
Militia armor is adequate in an ambush role with the lance as the hammer
disadvantages: The DropShip lifts the moment the convoy goes silent — with the hostages aboard
Loot crews are the Jacks' cheapest asset; the ship and the JumpShip connection survive untouched
Prisoners from a convoy fight know the ship's interior; getting them to say so takes time the dwell clock does not give
options.consequence: A won battle and a continued war. The convoy burns, the ship climbs, and the bonus schedule's hostage column stays empty for this cycle.

costs.resource: the hostage column forfeited this cycle: the ship lifts the moment the convoy goes silent
costs.risk: the ship and its JumpShip connection survive untouched — a won battle priced against a continued war

decisionPoints.name: The JumpShip Problem
decisionPoints.context: Somebody recharges the Jacks' JumpShip, and somebody reads them the packet schedule. The contract mentions neither. But the planet's future depends mostly on both.

options.title: Ignore It — Kill What Lands
advantages: Contract scope stays clean; every asset stays on the mission that pays
A dead or captured DropShip ends {WORLD}'s problem regardless of who recharged it
disadvantages: The JumpShip recruits a new DropShip within a season; the pattern restarts on a different world or this one
The schedule leak — whoever reads the packet timetable for them — stays in place, unfound
options.consequence: The local problem is solved locally. The regional problem sails on, and in a year another commission on another world writes the same contract.

costs.risk: the JumpShip recruits a new DropShip within a season — the pattern restarts on this world or the next

options.title: Charter the Mail Packet to Fix the Point
advantages: The packet's transit sensors, properly tasked, can confirm the nonstandard point in one loiter
A fixed recharge point converts the astronomer's rumor into an actionable naval target for whoever has a navy
disadvantages: Chartering the packet costs {WORLD} its only link for a full cycle: no mail, no market prices, no medical requisitions — the legislature must literally vote to buy silence
The packet is unarmed; if the Jacks' JumpShip notices the loiter, the planet's lifeline is the next casualty
options.consequence: The long war chosen over the short one. {WORLD} goes fully dark for a month to buy the one coordinate that makes the Jacks mortal — and lives with whatever needed mailing.

costs.resource: {WORLD}'s only off-world link: silent for a full packet cycle — no mail, no market prices, no medical requisitions
costs.risk: an unarmed packet loitering at a hot point — if the Jacks' JumpShip notices, the lifeline is the next casualty

options.title: Pass the Bearing Downstream by Courier
advantages: Costs nothing: the astronomer's log rides the next packet to the regional command's standing military liaison
Keeps the unit's force and the planet's lifeline intact and on mission
disadvantages: Two jumps, a month, a desk, a queue: the honest estimate is that nothing happens for two cycles, if ever
An uncalibrated single observation, forwarded without confirmation, is the easiest report in the Sphere to file and forget
options.consequence: Due diligence at the speed of the Dark Age. The paperwork is impeccable, the bearing goes into a folder, and the JumpShip's safety now depends entirely on how bored a regional analyst is that week.

costs.risk: an uncalibrated single observation, forwarded without confirmation, is the easiest report in the Sphere to file and forget

entries.event: Raider DropShip grounds on the salt hardpan; silo spotter network reports by field telephone.
First loot convoy rolls for the terminals — observed strength 8-12 vehicles plus escorting 'Mechs.
Convoy transits the cut, the only defile on the terminal road.
First convoy returns loaded; second convoy departs. The cycle repeats up to three times.
Final convoy recovery; ramp activity and pre-lift checks visible at the ship.
Earliest observed lift across three raids. The Hardpan is empty by T+7:15 at the latest.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Every phase of the chosen plan completes by T+6:00. At T+6:40 on the earliest observed pattern, that ship lifts — and there is no aerospace on this world to argue with it, no HPG to report it, and no help nearer than two jumps and a month.

opforSketch.composition: Pirate band, salvage-grade but maintained: a lance-equivalent of patched BattleMechs and heavy vehicles escorting loot convoys (Regular), technical vehicles and dismounts for loading (Green), one mixed-bay DropShip with functional bay weapons and a competent master. Generator should make the ship itself the hardest problem on the field — a grounded fortress with a launch option.
opforSketch.behavior: Clockwork raiding doctrine keyed to the packet cycle. Avoids peer engagement entirely: convoys withdraw to the ship at first serious contact, and the ship lifts early if threatened — hostages and cargo both aboard. Actual ground dwell this raid: {GROUND_DWELL} minutes, rolled within the observed pattern. Uses false IFF to delay every engagement decision made against it by 2-3 minutes, and knows it.

forks.name: OPERATION RETURN POST
forks.trigger: DropShip taken or destroyed with hostages recovered; nav core secured.
forks.consequence: The core fixes the renegade JumpShip's recharge point. The commission funds an intercept tasking — beyond contract scope, real naval risk, and the only chance to end the regional pattern instead of the local one. Optional, lucrative, and dangerous in that order.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY MAILBAG
forks.trigger: The Jacks lift untouched, or the strike misses the window entirely.
forks.consequence: The raid economics improve and word travels the raider circuit at JumpShip speed. The Jacks return at the next-plus-one cycle with a second DropShip and friends — and the planetary commission is now negotiating from a harvest that just got smaller.

forks.name: OPERATION SMALL PARCELS
forks.trigger: Convoy element destroyed but the ship escapes with hostages aboard.
forks.consequence: Within two cycles, a ransom contact arrives via the mail packet — terms, proof-of-life, a rendezvous two systems out. The follow-on is a negotiation with a gun under the table, conducted at the speed of JumpShip mail.

storyElementSeed: The spotter on the co-op silo cranks a field telephone older than her grandmother and reads a bearing off a sight she made from pipe stock. Two clicks on the line — received. Out on the flat, dust stands up where the air is otherwise still.

phases.name: PHASE I — THE QUIET CYCLE
phases.lead: Preparation runs between packet sailings, because the raid window does: positions dug, militia fire discipline drilled against the stale-IFF problem, and the silo telephone net rehearsed until a bearing moves from a crank handle to the gun line in under 4 minutes. Nothing goes out on radio that a scanner could sell; the plan moves by courier satchel and memory.

dataBlock.Salt hardpan: salt flat 70 km from the terminals; no approach cover for 11 km in any direction
dataBlock.Observed ground dwell: 6:40, 7:10, 6:55 across three raids (41 days old, medium confidence)
dataBlock.Raid window: opens when the mail packet sails; {WORLD} is mute for nearly 4 weeks
dataBlock.Spotter net: co-op silo watchers on hand-cranked field telephones; no aerospace, no satellite layer, no live registry
dataBlock.IFF hazard: raiders squawk military codes 2 years stale; nothing on-world can disprove them in real time

phases.name: PHASE II — GROUNDING DAY
phases.lead: From the first silo report the operation lives inside the dwell clock: the plan chosen at the decision annex executes complete by T+6:00, because at T+6:40 on the earliest observed pattern the ship lifts and nothing on {WORLD} can follow it. Orders issued in this phase are one clause long — the militia's radios are older than their crews, and the plan already knows it.

protocol.Sighting report: bearing and count by field telephone, read twice; two cranks on the line acknowledge — nothing on radio until contact is general
protocol.Identification rule: no fire before visual identification inside 500 m, transponders notwithstanding — the battery that holed the mail shuttle bought this rule, and the unit will not pay for it twice
protocol.Hostage call: codeword GRAIN TALLY freezes all fire onto the DropShip itself; boarding or surrender outcomes only while the count says they are aboard
protocol.Lift warning: ramp activity or drive pre-heat reported as LAST POST — every element checks its own clock against T+6:40 and acts on the plan, not on permission

sidebarKernel.kernel: Grounded, that ship is a fortress with a launch option: bay weapons, a competent master, and an engine bell that ends the argument the moment it lights. Take the ramp and the bridge or do not board at all — half a boarding party at lift-off is a hostage column of your own.

phases.name: PHASE III — THE LONG ACCOUNTING
phases.lead: What the afternoon leaves behind is settled at courier speed: hostages mustered against the co-op rolls, the navigation core copied before anyone with a competing claim arrives, and the JumpShip question answered per the decision annex — knowing the report travels two jumps in a mailbag, and the answer, if it ever comes, comes next season.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Whoever schedules these raids reads the packet timetable, and the timetable is posted at the terminal office for anyone to read. Start the counter-question locally: the list of people who knew the sailing date 3 days early is short, and it is written on paper nobody thought to hide.

assetDetails.detail: {HOSTAGES} workers, held aboard the DropShip as cargo labor. That comes from the released hostage's count, which is 38 days old and unconfirmed. During loading they work the ramp and the bay mouths, the one window when you can reach them without fighting through the hull. The bonus schedule pays per head alive; the town that is waiting counts the same way.

Co-op volunteers on hand-cranked telephones, reading bearings off pipe-stock sights. They are the operation's entire sensor layer and its softest point: if the Jacks ever learn where the bearings come from, the silos burn on the next raid. No spotter location appears in any written order, and the line-layout map exists in exactly 2 copies.

Already holed once by the militia battery on a bad IFF call. It flies the only schedule on the planet that matters; its approach windows are briefed to every gun crew by date and bearing, and any plan that puts fire near a descending transponder waits on the visual rule, every time.

resourceGates.lackingText: No forward base: water and thermal blinds stage from the terminals by night convoy — add 2 days to emplacement and one more movement pattern for anyone watching the flat to read.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Charter the Mail Packet to Fix the Point
resourceGates.lackingText: Option renders locked: COMMISSION FUNDING REQUIRED — charter escrow exceeds the treasury; a legislature vote adds an estimated 14 days, and the packet sails on schedule regardless.

title: OPERATION BORROWED CLOCK
skeleton: instructor must certify a green formation by a fixed inspection date while an unverifiable raid warning forces choosing between teaching the syllabus and digging in against a ghost, with no way to amend the result
inspiration: raising and certifying a militia under threat of imminent invasion (e.g. home-guard mobilization on a contested frontier, 1940)
situation:
{WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. This world remembers what {TARGET_FACTION} does when the realm is blind, and the realm has been blind for two years. With the HPG grid dark, every report from the border arrives by courier, two to four weeks out of date. The last intelligence digest was 24 days old when it landed and only moderately reliable; it placed a {TARGET_FACTION} probe staging two jumps out. The next digest will be the first real confirmation either way. In the gap between those two reports, {EMPLOYER} is re-raising the March militia, and your unit holds the cadre contract. Take {RECRUITS} recruits: co-op drivers, mine techs, and cargo handlers from the dropport, 41 of them with prior service. Certify a combat-capable battalion in 75 days, when the March command courier returns with an inspection team and the new digest. You are training against a clock you cannot read. The enemy may arrive before the news does. That one sentence is the whole strategic picture of the year, and a copy of it is taped inside your operations tent.

The terrain problem is the bottoms: 14 kilometers of seasonal floodplain between the training grounds and the city approach. In the dry season it is the only flat ground large enough for a battalion-scale landing, which means any competent attacker will use it, which means the militia has to learn to fight on it. The floods arrive around day {FLOOD_DAY} and flip the problem — the bottoms become a water obstacle and your maneuver area drowns. The training schedule works around the river or it fails.

The friction, itemized. Equipment is salvage-grade: small arms at full issue, support weapons at 55 percent of establishment, 4 of 12 promised APCs delivered. There have been {FALSE_ALARMS} false invasion scares planet-wide in 60 days; each muster costs two training days and a measurable desertion tick, because you cannot disprove a rumor by checking a network that no longer exists. Two baronial households insist their retainers train as separate platoons, and the writ that would override them is — like everything else — five weeks away by courier. {NPC:employer-contact} is working the problem at the March court; expect nothing soon.

Certification day is unforgiving. The courier's DropShip holds orbit for 18 hours, takes the inspection report aboard either way, and whatever the battalion is that morning is what the March believes it has all winter. In the Dark Age, a mistake lasts exactly as long as the communication loop.

objectives.primary: Certify the battalion combat-capable at the day-75 inspection: gunnery, field movement, and a battalion-level defensive exercise on the bottoms.
objectives.secondary: Build the defensive plan the battalion will actually fight: surveyed positions, range cards, and flood-season variants for the Bottoms approach.
objectives.bonus: Zero desertion among the 41 prior-service cadre candidates — they are the NCO corps this battalion keeps after you leave.

complications.name: Salvage-Grade Issue
complications.text: Support weapons at 55 percent, 4 of 12 APCs, and optics that were obsolete before the Blackout. The battalion trains on what it will fight with, which is at least honest.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Militia units carry equipment-deficit ratings until shortfalls resolve; live-fire training above squad level consumes the same scarce stocks the war plan needs. Track both against the same ledger.

complications.name: Rumor Musters
complications.text: A freighter crew's story, a light on the horizon, a barony's panicked landline — each one a planet-wide muster nobody can veto, because the one time it is real, the veto is the headline.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll for false-alarm events through the campaign: each costs 2 training days and a 1-3 percent desertion tick. The day-40 alarm (see decision point) is scripted and arrives regardless.

complications.name: The Baronial Platoons
complications.text: Two households train their retainers apart, under their own colors, pending a writ that is weeks away at best. The retainers are decent material. The arrangement is a fracture line wearing livery.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Until resolved (writ arrival roll, or a negotiated integration), the two platoons fight as separate units with a coordination penalty and cannot anchor the battalion exercise.

complications.name: The River Does Not Read the Syllabus
complications.text: Flood season arrives around day {FLOOD_DAY}, give or take ten. Every maneuver lesson the Bottoms can teach must be taught before the water takes the classroom back.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Roll flood arrival. After flood: the Bottoms maneuver area is closed, battalion exercises move to the constrained upland grounds, and the defensive problem flips from open-field to water-obstacle doctrine mid-syllabus.

decisionPoints.name: Curriculum
decisionPoints.context: Seventy-five days produces exactly one battalion. What kind of battalion is decided in the first week and paid for in the last.

options.title: Broad Combined-Arms Basics
advantages: Certain to certify 'adequate' across every inspection category
Produces a militia useful for the planet's actual daily needs: convoys, checkpoints, flood relief
No category failure can sink the inspection
disadvantages: Masters nothing; an actual {TARGET_FACTION} probe meets a battalion that is uniformly mediocre at resisting it
The 41 prior-service candidates stagnate teaching basics they already know
options.consequence: The safe certificate. The March gets a militia battalion in the median of the curve, and the curve was drawn in peacetime.

costs.resource: the 41 prior-service candidates stagnate teaching basics they already know
costs.risk: a real {TARGET_FACTION} probe meets a battalion uniformly mediocre at resisting it

options.title: Anti-'Mech Focus
advantages: Trains against the threat that actually ends worlds: infantry that can live near hostile BattleMechs and hurt them
The Bottoms' dry-season geometry is the ideal classroom for exactly this
If the digest was right, this is the only curriculum that mattered
disadvantages: Patrol, convoy, and policing skills go untaught; the planet's daily security needs stay unmet for a season
Anti-'Mech training is casualty-prone even done well: expect training injuries the recruiting ledger feels
If the probe never comes, the inspection grades a narrow battalion against a broad rubric
options.consequence: A bet on the digest. Right, and {WORLD}'s militia is the rare one that can stand on its own ground. Wrong, and the certificate reads 'specialized' where the March wanted 'ready.'

costs.resource: training injuries: anti-'Mech instruction done well still hospitalizes recruits the rosters feel
costs.risk: if the probe never comes, the inspection grades a narrow battalion against a broad rubric

options.title: Live Cadre-Led Operations in the Upland Hills
advantages: The bandit camps in the uplands are a real enemy at instructional scale: live patrols, live contact, live consequences
Nothing builds NCOs faster; the 41 become leaders in weeks instead of months
Clears an actual security problem the baronies have complained about for two years
disadvantages: Real casualties among trainees, before certification, with names — the training rosters get shorter and the town knows why
Operational tempo eats syllabus time; the inspection rubric does not award marks for cleared camps
A bad contact early can break the battalion's confidence before it exists
options.consequence: The fastest path to soldiers, paid in advance. By day 75 the battalion has a war record or a wound, and the difference was decided in the uplands, out of your control.

costs.resource: trainee casualties before certification, with names the town knows
costs.risk: one bad contact early breaks the battalion's confidence before the battalion exists

decisionPoints.name: The Day-40 Alarm
decisionPoints.context: A freighter crew swears to drive flares at a pirate point, 19 days ago, profiles consistent with military DropShips. No confirmation exists, and none can: the network that would confirm it has been a grey tile for two years.

options.title: Disperse to War Positions
advantages: If it is real, the battalion meets it dug in on surveyed ground instead of in barracks
The dispersal is itself the best battalion-level exercise the syllabus contains
Politically unimpeachable: nobody is ever court-martialed for taking the threat seriously
disadvantages: Nine training days lost if false — and at day 40, nine days is the difference between certifying and not
A false-alarm dispersal feeds the desertion tick harder than any rumor: the recruits' farms are mid-harvest
options.consequence: The battalion learns its ground and loses its margin. If the flares were freighters, certification day arrives against a syllabus that is nine days short.

costs.resource: desertion: a mid-harvest dispersal feeds the tick harder than any rumor
costs.risk: nine of the thirty-five remaining training days spent on a freighter crew's story

options.title: Send the Cadre Recon to Verify
advantages: The only option that produces information instead of consuming schedule
If real, you know first — days before the courier loop could tell anyone anything
The battalion's training continues uninterrupted under junior instructors
disadvantages: Your instructors — the contract's entire value — are 8 days gone on a maybe
If contact comes while they are out, the battalion meets it leaderless and half-trained
A verification mission against real {TARGET_FACTION} pathfinders is a combat mission wearing a clipboard
options.consequence: Information bought with the cadre's presence. The syllabus survives on momentum, and for 8 days the contract's success rides in a recon vehicle pointed at a rumor.

costs.resource: the instructors — the contract's entire value — gone 8 days on a maybe
costs.risk: if contact comes meanwhile, the battalion meets it leaderless and half-trained

options.title: Log It and Train On
advantages: The syllabus holds; day 75 arrives with every planned lesson taught
Refusing to feed the rumor economy steadies a planet that has mustered {FALSE_ALARMS} times for nothing
Statistically the correct call: every alarm so far has been weather, freighters, or nerves
disadvantages: If it is real, the battalion meets it in barracks formation with 35 days of training, and the inquiry afterward reads this log entry aloud
The recruits know the report exists; training under an unanswered question has its own attrition
options.consequence: Discipline as a wager. The clock you cannot read keeps running, and the decision is filed where the inquiry — or nobody — will find it.

costs.risk: if the flares were real, the battalion meets them in barracks formation — and the inquiry reads this log entry aloud

entries.event: Unverified landing report reaches cadre HQ — freighter crew interview logged at the DropPort.
Planetary command requests militia readiness state; the request is also a political question.
Recall riders reach outlying training companies — motorcycles and landlines, because nothing else exists.
Battalion assembled at war positions, if dispersal was ordered; otherwise musters complete at the training grounds.
Second freighter-crew interview contradicts the first, or fails to. The report is now exactly as verified as it will ever be.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Day 75, 0900: the certification inspection begins when the courier grounds. The DropShip holds orbit 18 hours and embarks the report either way. Whatever the battalion is that morning is what the March believes it has all winter — the result rides a 5-week communication loop and cannot be amended from here.

opforSketch.composition: Training threat: bandit groups in the upland hills — light vehicles, dismounts, no BattleMechs (Green). Conditional threat: a {TARGET_FACTION} probe per the digest — estimated battalion combat team with a BattleMech company core (Regular/Veteran), arriving by DropShip on the floodplain hardstand if it arrives at all. Generator should hold the probe behind the campaign gate, not the encounter table.
opforSketch.behavior: Bandits avoid contact with anything organized and prey on what is not. The probe, if real, follows reconnaissance-in-force doctrine: seize the floodplain hardstand, test the defense's composition and resolve, and withdraw rather than bleed — unless the defense collapses, in which case the probe stops being a probe.

forks.name: OPERATION FIRST WATCH
forks.trigger: Battalion certified at day 75 with cadre NCO corps intact.
forks.consequence: When the probe comes — and the winter digest says it comes — the militia holds the bottoms long enough for the line battalion to deploy. {EMPLOYER} offers the cadre unit the line-support contract for that fight, on the strength of a battalion that stood where it was trained to.

forks.name: OPERATION REARGUARD SCHOOL
forks.trigger: Certification failed, or the probe arrives before day 75.
forks.consequence: The cadre covers the withdrawal of a half-trained battalion across the flooding bottoms — instructors fighting the demonstration they never got to teach, with the inspection team's DropShip as the only ride out for the wounded.

forks.name: OPERATION CIRCUIT RIDER
forks.trigger: The day-75 digest reports the {TARGET_FACTION} probe redirected elsewhere.
forks.consequence: March command, reading the certification report, contracts the cadre to repeat the program on two more border worlds. In a Sphere without HPGs, a training syllabus that works travels the only way anything travels now: by ship, with the people who wrote it.

storyElementSeed: Evening class. A recruit who drove grain trucks for eleven years learns to read a paper map by red light, because the satellite layer has been a grey tile for two years and nobody is coming to fix it.

phases.name: INTAKE (DAYS 1-20)
phases.lead: Sorting before teaching: the 41 prior-service candidates are identified, interviewed, and salted through the companies as acting NCOs in the first week, because everything after depends on them. The equipment ledger is signed for as found — 55 percent of establishment is the truth, and the syllabus is built on the truth rather than on the consignment promises.

dataBlock.Issue state: small arms full; support weapons 55 percent; 4 of 12 promised APCs delivered
dataBlock.Clock: 75 days to inspection; courier DropShip holds orbit 18 hours
dataBlock.Flood: the bottoms close around day {FLOOD_DAY}, give or take ten
dataBlock.Comms: couriers, landlines, and motorcycles — the intelligence picture is 24 days old on arrival and ages from there

phases.name: THE FLOODPLAIN WINDOW (DAYS 21 TO THE FLOOD)
phases.lead: Every lesson the floodplain can teach is taught before the river takes the classroom back: battalion movement, surveyed positions, range cards for the one hardstand a competent attacker must use. The day-40 alarm lands in this window — see the decision annex — and the syllabus carries a 9-day contingency that the staff guards like ammunition.

protocol.Recall: muster orders move by motorcycle rider and baronial landline, in that order; riders carry written orders — nothing of substance goes by voice on lines the baronies share
protocol.Alarm grading: every invasion report is logged with source, age, and the one question that matters: could anyone confirm this if it were true? On {WORLD} in the Blackout the honest answer is no — the grading is about cost, not truth
protocol.Muster accounting: each false alarm closes out with a written cost line: training days lost, desertion tick, stocks expended — and the committee of one that signs it is the cadre commander

sidebarKernel.kernel: The digest is 24 days old and the next one arrives with the inspection. Treat every report in between as a weather forecast: plan against the range of it, never against the middle — and write down what you assumed, because the inquiry, if there is one, will be conducted by people with a working calendar.

phases.name: CERTIFICATION (DAYS 60-75)
phases.lead: The last fortnight rehearses the battalion exercise on whichever ground the river has left, against the standard the inspection team will actually apply. Day 75, 0900: the courier grounds, holds orbit 18 hours, and embarks the report either way — whatever the battalion is that morning is what the March believes it has all winter.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Certify the battalion you built, not the one the rubric imagines: brief the inspectors on the 55 percent ledger and the flood-shortened syllabus in the first ten minutes, in writing. A militia that is honestly average is useful; a paper-strong one gets spent like the real thing.

assetDetails.detail: The battalion's future NCO corps and the bonus clause in human form. 9 hold harvest-exemption appeals pending at the baronial courts; a mid-harvest dispersal or a denied appeal is the likeliest desertion trigger among them. Acting rank in week one, confirmed rank at certification — promised in writing, because in the Blackout a verbal promise from an off-world unit is worth its postage.

Two households, training apart under their own colors pending a writ that is 5 weeks away at best. The retainers are decent material with better equipment than the line companies; the households read every integration order as precedent. Integrate them through tasks, not directives — joint live-fire details first, the org chart last.
